title: Excelsior on the Park Reviews: Pros, Cons and Rents
seo_title: Excelsior on the Park Reviews: Pros & Cons
description: Read Excelsior on the Park reviews from renters: roomy townhome-style units and low rents vs. pest, maintenance, and gate issues. See what to check first.
excerpt: Located at 14300 Ella Blvd, Houston, TX 77014, Excelsior on the Park Apartments offers a mix of affordability, spacious layouts, and wooded surroundings. With a park-like setting, walking trails, and updated interiors, it caters to renters looking for space and value in the North Houston area. But with a current Google rating of 3.4 stars, […]
content:
Excelsior on the Park reviews paint a split picture: renters love the big floor plans, townhome-style layouts, and wooded setting at a budget-friendly price, but many also report pests, slow maintenance, and broken security gates. At the time of writing, the community at 14300 Ella Blvd in North Houston held a 3.4-star Google rating.

Below, we break down the property details, what residents praise, what they complain about, and the questions worth asking before you sign a lease.

Excelsior on the Park at a glance

Excelsior on the Park sits in the North Houston area near Greenspoint. It's an older community, built in 1983 and updated over time, with roughly 200 units spread across a park-like, wooded campus with walking paths.

DetailWhat the community lists
Address14300 Ella Blvd, Houston, TX 77014
Approximate unit count200
Year built1983, with updates over time
Floor plans1, 2, and 3 bedrooms, including townhome-style layouts
Google rating3.4 stars (at the time of writing)
Pet policyDogs and cats allowed, with breed and weight restrictions; pet rent and fees apply

Recently listed rents

Rents at the time of writing were among the more affordable in the area:

  • 1 bedroom: from the high $900s
  • 2 bedrooms: from the low $1,200s
  • 3 bedrooms: from the high $1,600s

Pricing shifts with availability, lease length, and upgrades, so confirm current numbers with the leasing office.

Advertised amenities and services

  • Two swimming pools
  • Fitness center
  • Clubhouse and business center
  • Tennis court and playground
  • Gated, controlled access
  • Laundry facilities
  • BBQ and picnic areas
  • Wooded surroundings with walking paths
  • Balconies or patios in select units
  • On-site management and maintenance, plus an online resident portal

The community also markets "apartminium" layouts, park views, outdoor social spaces, and townhome options. Keep in mind that several reviewers say some of these amenities were closed or not working, which we cover below.

What residents like about Excelsior on the Park

Staff who make a difference

A number of reviewers complimented the staff for respectful, helpful treatment during move-in. Some credited the management team with improving their quality of life and helping them feel safe and cared for.

One review described a staff member who made sure a wheelchair-accessible unit was ready and that maintenance was handled promptly. Another resident said they renewed their lease specifically because of changes brought in by new property management. Others called the leasing office warm and welcoming.

The common thread: service seems to depend heavily on who is running the property at the time. When management is responsive, residents notice.

Spacious floor plans and a quieter setting

Unit size is the most consistent compliment. Residents mentioned roomy layouts, large patios, big bedrooms, and two-story townhome-style designs. One reviewer called the apartments "breathtaking" after touring a 2- or 3-bedroom unit.

The green, wooded grounds also stood out, giving the property a calmer feel than many Houston complexes. Some residents described the community as mostly peaceful, with only the occasional noise from kids or pets.

Value for the square footage

Even reviewers who listed problems often acknowledged that rent is competitive for the region. Several said they chose Excelsior mainly for its budget-friendly leases and accepted some trade-offs. Families and single parents in particular pointed to the value-for-space ratio, and despite the property's age, residents described the interiors as decently updated.

Common complaints in Excelsior on the Park reviews

Pests and cleanliness

The most repeated complaint involved roaches, rats, and raccoons. Several residents described pest problems as persistent even with pest control service. One tenant said their unit stayed infested no matter how clean they kept it; others mentioned raccoons in the attic, rat sightings, and dirty shared spaces such as the pools and trash areas.

One detailed review described moldy ceilings, raccoon feces on balconies, and a broken lighting system labeled a fire hazard.

Slow maintenance

Many reviewers said maintenance requests went unanswered for weeks or even months. Reported issues included broken A/C units, malfunctioning refrigerators, and electrical concerns. Several tenants said they had to follow up repeatedly or visit the office in person, and a few were told to buy their own materials, such as door sealants, to fix problems.

Some renters said they moved out because unresolved repairs, including faulty wiring, mold, and pest damage, made them feel unsafe.

Security gates and amenity closures

Broken gates and malfunctioning cameras came up often. Residents said the gates stayed open around the clock and that there was little visible security. Several reviews mentioned break-ins, stolen cars, and mailbox theft.

Another recurring theme: advertised amenities that were non-functional or closed, including the pools, laundry rooms, fitness center, and a tennis court that reportedly had no net. One resident said they were paying over $1,100 a month and still lacked a working mailbox, functioning gates, or clean common areas.

Pros and cons of Excelsior on the Park

ProsCons
Large, open floor plansPersistent pest problems reported by multiple tenants
Townhome-style optionsDelayed or ignored maintenance requests
Quiet, park-like surroundingsBroken gates and camera systems
Affordable rent for the square footageAmenity closures and poor upkeep
Some excellent staff and managementInconsistent management over time

Is Excelsior on the Park right for you?

Excelsior on the Park can work for renters who want more space for less money and who are comfortable advocating for repairs. If security, cleanliness, fast maintenance, and fully working amenities are top priorities, you may want to compare other options, or at least inspect your exact unit carefully first.

Experiences here vary a lot by building, unit, and the management team in place. Before you sign:

  1. Tour the specific unit you'll lease, not a model, and check under sinks and in closets for signs of pests or leaks.
  2. Ask whether the gates, pools, laundry, and gym are currently working.
  3. Ask how maintenance requests are submitted and what the typical turnaround is.
  4. Visit in the evening to get a feel for parking and security.
  5. Get any promised repairs or move-in conditions in writing.

If you're weighing similar budget-friendly communities, our Settegast Heights Village reviews are a useful comparison, and you can browse Houston apartments under $1,200 or 3-bedroom apartments for families who need room.

Frequently asked questions

What floor plans does Excelsior on the Park offer?

The community offers 1-, 2-, and 3-bedroom apartments, including townhome-style layouts. Some units have large patios or balconies and spacious bedrooms.

How much is rent at Excelsior on the Park?

At the time of writing, 1-bedrooms started in the high $900s, 2-bedrooms in the low $1,200s, and 3-bedrooms in the high $1,600s. Prices vary with availability, lease length, and upgrades.

Is Excelsior on the Park pet friendly?

Yes. Dogs and cats are allowed with breed and weight restrictions, and pet deposits, fees, and monthly pet rent apply. Our pet-friendly Houston apartments search can help you compare policies.

Is Excelsior on the Park a gated community?

It has gated access, but several reviews say the gates are often broken or left open, which is a common security concern among residents.

How responsive is maintenance?

Reviews are mixed. Some residents report quick, helpful service, while others describe waiting weeks or months for repairs. Ask the office about current response times before you lease.

Disclaimer: This article summarizes public Google reviews for Excelsior on the Park Apartments at 14300 Ella Blvd, Houston, TX 77014, which averaged 3.4 stars at the time of writing. Reviews reflect individual experiences, and conditions, pricing, and management can change. Contact the leasing office for current information.

title: The Henry at Lake Houston Reviews: What Residents Really Say

Nestled in a scenic and rapidly growing neighborhood just northeast of Houston, this upscale multifamily property offers a variety of modern amenities, spacious floor plans, and proximity to Lake Houston’s natural beauty. content:
Reading The Henry at Lake Houston reviews is the quickest way to see past the brochure: residents consistently praise the leasing staff, the layouts, and the location, while the most common complaints center on pests, parking and towing, and management turnover. At the time of writing, the community held an average Google rating of 4.1 out of 5 stars.

Below, we break down what this Humble, TX community offers, what residents love, what frustrates them, and the questions worth asking before you sign.

Disclaimer: This summary is based on Google reviews and reflects the opinions and experiences of residents and visitors. The 4.1-star average was accurate at the time of posting and may change.

The Henry at Lake Houston at a Glance

The Henry at Lake Houston is located at 14100 Will Clayton Pkwy, Humble, TX 77346, in a fast-growing area northeast of Houston near Lake Houston. If you are comparing communities in this part of town, our guide to apartments in Humble, TX is a good next stop.

Floor plans and recent pricing

Pricing below was estimated at the time of writing. Rents change with availability, lease term, and season, so treat these as a starting point, not a quote.

Floor planApprox. sizeRecently listed rent (estimated)
1 bed / 1 bath688–925 sq. ft.$1,100–$1,500+
2 bed / 2 bath1,064–1,184 sq. ft.$1,500–$1,800+
3 bed / 2 bath1,393 sq. ft.$1,900–$2,200+

Pet policy

  • Cats and dogs allowed
  • Up to two pets per apartment
  • Breed and weight restrictions may apply
  • Pet fees and monthly pet rent required

If pets are a must, you can also browse pet-friendly Houston apartments to compare policies side by side.

Amenities

  • Resort-style swimming pool
  • Fitness center
  • Clubhouse and resident lounge
  • Business center
  • Outdoor grilling and picnic areas
  • Door-to-door trash service (see our roundup of Houston apartments with valet trash)
  • Garages and covered parking available
  • Storage options
  • Private balconies or patios in many units
  • Granite countertops and stainless steel appliances

What Residents Love About The Henry at Lake Houston

Friendly, professional office staff

The staff is the most consistently praised part of the community. Several residents single out Ana, Tania, and Lauren by name:

"Ana and Lauren went above and beyond to help me during a stressful transition. They were empathetic, professional, and made me feel truly valued." — 5 stars

"Tania is very professional and will explain your billing in detail. Lauren really cares about the property." — 5 stars

"Ana is super friendly, knowledgeable, and made the leasing process smooth." — 5 stars

Clean grounds and quick maintenance (for some)

Some long-term residents say the community stays clean and that work orders get handled efficiently:

"I've lived here 2 years and it's always clean. Maintenance requests are handled quickly." — 5 stars

Convenient location and spacious layouts

Residents like having H-E-B, Kroger, Costco, and Walmart nearby, and they appreciate the modern floor plans:

"Location is spectacular. Layouts are unique and spacious. I'd live here again." — 4 stars

Common Complaints in The Henry at Lake Houston Reviews

The critical reviews follow a clear pattern: pest control, parking and towing, and changes in management.

Pest control issues

Multiple reviews describe spiders and insects in breezeways, stairwells, and even the pool area:

"The stairwells are full of bugs and spider webs. I've had to buy my own spray to feel safe walking out of my building." — 1 star

"Building 15 has black widows and spider nests. Even the pool chairs have spiders. This has been ignored for months." — 1 star

"Roaches, spiders, and silverfish are a common sight now. Pest control visits don't seem to help." — 4 stars

Parking and towing

Residents report limited visitor parking and towing, including vehicles registered to tenants:

"Visitor parking is limited and you're constantly worried about getting towed." — 1 star

"They towed vehicles registered to tenants. Management refuses to take accountability." — 1 star

This matters most for households with more than one car or anyone who hosts guests often.

Management turnover and new fees

Some residents mention as many as four management companies in a couple of years, along with policy changes and added fees:

"We've had 4 different management companies. Access to the gym was removed. Rent has to be paid in person by check." — 4 stars

"New management introduced fees for services we don't even use, like pool Wi-Fi and stormwater." — 4 stars

Some residents also note the community is not gated, which raised package security and safety concerns for them.

Pros and Cons Summary

ProsCons
Courteous, helpful office staffPest problems in breezeways and stairwells
Close to shopping, dining, and Lake HoustonLimited guest parking and towing concerns
Modern finishes and spacious layoutsManagement turnover and shifting policies
Resort-style amenitiesUnexpected or rarely used fees
Generally quiet, peaceful atmosphereInconsistent upkeep in shared areas

Is The Henry at Lake Houston Worth It?

For residents who land a well-kept unit and work with the right team members, the experience can be excellent: good layouts, a strong amenity package, and a convenient Humble location. The recurring complaints about pests, parking enforcement, and management changes are worth investigating before you commit.

Before you sign, we recommend you:

  • Tour the specific building and walk the stairwells and breezeways yourself.
  • Ask for the current guest parking and towing policy in writing.
  • Request a full list of monthly fees, including any amenity or utility add-ons.
  • Ask how rent can be paid and how often pest control services each building.
  • Talk with a current resident or two if you get the chance.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is The Henry at Lake Houston's Google rating?

At the time of writing, the community had an average Google rating of 4.1 out of 5 stars.

Does The Henry at Lake Houston allow pets?

Yes. Cats and dogs are allowed, up to two pets per apartment, with possible breed and weight restrictions, pet fees, and monthly pet rent.

Are there pest problems at The Henry at Lake Houston?

Some residents report spiders, roaches, and silverfish, especially in breezeways and stairwells. Pest control is provided, but reviews suggest results vary by building, so ask about the service schedule for the unit you are considering.

How is parking at The Henry at Lake Houston?

Resident parking is generally available, and garages and covered parking are offered, but many reviews mention limited guest parking and towing concerns.

Is The Henry at Lake Houston gated?

According to resident feedback, the community is not gated, which some tenants say affects package security.

title: Settegast Heights Village Reviews: An Honest Look at Life There

description: Settegast Heights Village reviews summarized: what renters say about safety, maintenance and management, plus its rare 4- and 5-bedroom units. Read first.
excerpt: When searching for a new place to call home in Houston, it’s essential to understand both the strengths and challenges of any potential apartment community. One property that has gained a fair share of attention and a mix of opinions is Settegast Heights Village, located at 7373 N Wayside Dr, Houston, TX 77028. With an […]
content:
Settegast Heights Village reviews tell the story of a Northeast Houston community in transition: big, budget-friendly floor plans and family amenities on one side, and serious complaints about safety, maintenance and management on the other. The property sits at 7373 N Wayside Dr, Houston, TX 77028, and held an overall Google rating of 3.1 stars at the time of writing.

Below, we break down what residents and visitors actually said, what the community offers on paper, and the questions we would ask before signing a lease here.

Disclaimer: All reviews and insights in this article were gathered from public Google Reviews at the time of writing. They reflect the personal experiences and opinions of residents and visitors. The 3.1-star overall rating was accurate as of the original publication date.

Settegast Heights Village at a glance

Settegast Heights Village is a garden-style, low-rise apartment community in Northeast Houston. It was built in 1973 and has approximately 200 units, with 1-, 2-, 3-, 4- and even 5-bedroom layouts. That range is what sets it apart for larger households.

DetailWhat we found
Address7373 N Wayside Dr, Houston, TX 77028
StyleGarden-style, low-rise
Year built1973
SizeApproximately 200 units
Floor plans1 to 5 bedrooms
RentHistorically reported between about $600 and $1,200 per month depending on unit size (at the time of writing)
PetsDogs and cats allowed; specific policies not publicly detailed
ParkingOn-site surface parking; no assigned or garage parking listed
Google rating3.1 stars at the time of writing

Amenities

  • On-site laundry facilities
  • Playground
  • Basketball court
  • Swimming pool
  • Outdoor gathering spaces

The community markets itself as family-focused, with outdoor amenities and spacious units designed for multi-generational living. Here is how residents describe the reality.

Positive Settegast Heights Village reviews

The good reviews are fewer, but they point to real progress and to one genuine advantage: space.

A cleaner, more controlled community than before

One reviewer said the community has improved significantly from its troubled past, crediting a strict curfew policy with creating a more orderly environment.

“This used to be a drug-infested apartment complex… They’ve cleaned this place up. They actually have a curfew and they’re pretty strict with that policy. It’s been a long time coming, but change has come.”

That suggests a visible effort to enforce rules, even if residents agree there is still work to do.

Family-oriented outdoor amenities

Reviews rarely mention the amenities in detail, but a playground, basketball court and pool give kids and families somewhere to go without leaving the property. If those spaces matter to you, walk them during your tour and check their condition yourself.

Rare 4- and 5-bedroom apartments

Four- and five-bedroom apartments are uncommon in Houston, especially at this price point. For a large family that needs bedrooms more than finishes, that alone can put Settegast Heights Village on the shortlist. If you need fewer bedrooms, you can also browse 3-bedroom apartments across Houston for comparison.

Negative Settegast Heights Village reviews

Most of the reviews we sampled raise critical issues with safety, cleanliness, maintenance and management, and the consistency of those complaints is hard to ignore.

Safety and crime concerns

Several reviewers described serious safety problems, including violent incidents and fatalities, and felt the office’s response was ineffective.

“Young men got killed over an argument… people dying over here every day and the office isn’t following proper procedure.”

“People are rude here, mean, and violent. I’ve lived in this neighborhood my whole life.”

For families, these reports raise immediate questions about children’s well-being and the general security of residents.

Maintenance neglect and health hazards

Residents reported slow or absent responses to essential repairs, including air conditioning and mold, along with pest problems.

“Maintenance doesn’t fix anything just lets the mold build up. Roaches and rats running in and out of people’s apartments.”

“My air is out, I’ve called six times, and no one has responded. My child has bad nosebleeds and can’t breathe.”

In Houston’s heat and humidity, a broken AC or untreated mold is more than an inconvenience, especially for children and older adults.

Management issues and alleged harassment

Many reviewers described office staff as rude, unprofessional and unresponsive, and some said they were targeted after raising concerns.

“The new manager is rude, doesn’t know how to talk to people, and lies on paperwork. I reported sexual harassment and ever since, I’ve been harassed and my kids targeted.”

“They lie, push you to move out, and some residents who’ve been here for years act like they run everything.”

Towing

One reviewer said their car was towed multiple times in a month despite proper registration, which points to parking rules that are either aggressively enforced or poorly communicated.

“Got my car towed three times in one month — ridiculous.”

An unwelcoming atmosphere

Some visitors described the social environment as cold.

“I speak to the residents when I visit they don’t even speak back. I feel like this place is cursed.”

Rating snapshot from 10 sampled Google reviews

Star ratingNumber of reviews
5 stars0
4 stars1
3 stars2
2 stars0
1 star7

Seven of the 10 recent reviews we sampled were 1-star ratings. One was 4 stars, two were 3 stars, and none were 5 stars.

Who Settegast Heights Village may suit

May be a fit forMay not be ideal for
Large families needing budget-friendly 4- or 5-bedroom apartmentsRenters who want a quiet, secure, professionally managed community
Renters who value space over updated finishesFamilies worried about mold, pests or broken AC
Residents prepared to actively push for repairs and oversightAnyone who expects consistent customer service and fast issue resolution

How to vet Settegast Heights Village before you sign

  1. Visit at different times of day, including evenings and weekends, to get a feel for the grounds and parking.
  2. Talk to current residents away from the leasing office if you can.
  3. Ask about maintenance response times and how emergency AC calls are handled in summer.
  4. Ask about security measures and the curfew policy reviewers mentioned.
  5. Get the towing and guest parking rules in writing before move-in.
  6. Inspect the exact unit for signs of moisture, mold and pests, not just a model.

If affordability is what brought you here, it is worth comparing a few other options too. Our guide to tax credit apartments in Houston and our apartments under $1,200 search are good places to start.

Frequently asked questions

What is the rent at Settegast Heights Village?

Rent has historically been reported between about $600 and $1,200 per month depending on unit size. Prices change, so confirm current rates and availability with the leasing office.

What floor plans does Settegast Heights Village offer?

The community offers 1-, 2-, 3-, 4- and 5-bedroom units, which makes it one of the few options for very large households.

Is Settegast Heights Village pet-friendly?

Yes, dogs and cats are allowed, but specific breed restrictions and fees were not publicly detailed. Ask for the written pet policy before applying. You can also search pet-friendly Houston apartments.

What are the most common complaints in Settegast Heights Village reviews?

Reviewers most often mention slow maintenance, mold and pests, safety concerns, towing and unprofessional management.

Has Settegast Heights Village improved?

Some reviewers noted visible improvements, such as a strict curfew and a cleaner property, but many still report ongoing problems.

title: Revl Heights Reviews: Resident Pros, Cons, Rent and Fees

description: Revl Heights reviews from residents: rents, pet fees, and amenities, plus the garage security and towing complaints to ask about before you tour.
excerpt: Choosing a new place to live is a big decision especially in a vibrant and competitive city like Houston. If you’re considering Revl Heights, located at 825 Usener St, Houston, TX 77009, then you’re probably looking for a balanced perspective on what life there is really like. With a strong Google rating of 4.4 stars, […]
content:
Revl Heights reviews paint a picture of a stylish, amenity-packed mid-rise at 825 Usener St, just minutes from downtown, with a 4.4-star Google rating at the time of writing. Residents love the leasing team, the finishes, and the views, while the most common complaints center on garage security, guest towing, and maintenance follow-up. Here is what renters are saying, plus the rents, fees, and features you should know before you tour.

Note: The opinions summarized here come from publicly available Google Reviews and reflect individual resident experiences at the time they were posted. The 4.4-star rating was current when this article was published and may change over time.

Revl Heights at a glance

Revl Heights is an upscale mid-rise community built in 2016 in the Woodland Heights area, close to the restaurants and parks that draw renters to the Houston Heights area. It has 326 units, from one-bedrooms to larger two-bedroom layouts, ranging from 648 to 1,452 sq ft.

DetailWhat we found
Address825 Usener St, Houston, TX 77009
Year built2016
Units326 (one- and two-bedroom)
Unit sizes648 to 1,452 sq ft
Rent range$1,463 to $2,804/month at the time of writing, depending on floor plan
Google rating4.4 stars at publication
Assigned garage parking$40/month
EV charging$60/month

Pet policy

  • Cats and dogs allowed
  • Maximum of 2 pets per unit
  • $400 non-refundable pet fee
  • $25/month pet rent
  • On-site dog park and pet spa

If you are comparing pet policies across the city, our pet-friendly Houston apartments search makes it easy to line up fees side by side.

Apartment features and community amenities

Revl Heights positions itself as a high-end rental, and the feature list backs that up. It is one of the stronger amenity packages in the area, especially if smart-home touches matter to you.

Inside the apartments

  • 10-foot ceilings with vaulted layouts
  • Google Nest smart thermostats
  • Quartz countertops, kitchen islands, and wine chillers (wine chillers in select units)
  • Stainless steel appliances and French door refrigerators
  • Full-size washer and dryer in every unit
  • Frameless showers with bench seating (select units)
  • Engineered wood and tile flooring
  • Walk-in closets, custom cabinetry, and garden tubs

Community perks

  • Resort-style pool with an outdoor kitchen and grills
  • Sky Lounge with panoramic city views
  • Yoga and spin room with Fitness on Demand, plus a 24-hour fitness center
  • Dog park and pet spa
  • EV charging stations ($60/month) and assigned garage parking ($40/month)
  • Business center, library, and conference room
  • Controlled-access gates and video surveillance
  • Valet trash, dry cleaning, a guest suite, and planned resident events

Positive Revl Heights reviews

Many residents praise Revl Heights for its professional staff, modern features, and fast leasing process. Several reviewers said they were impressed from the first tour.

Fast leasing and helpful staff

The application and move-in process comes up again and again as quick and smooth, and leasing agents Ayron and Jackie were praised by name.

"I'm so impressed with how fast and efficient the look, apply, and lease process has been. Ayron has been exceptional since the moment I came to look at the unit. From start to finish took 3 days!" (5 stars)

"Had an amazing experience from start to finish with Jackie! She made the entire move-in process incredibly smooth and stress-free. The whole staff was welcoming, helpful, and very understanding." (5 stars)

Design, views, and location

Reviewers like the downtown views, the quiet neighborhood, and the high-end feel of the property. The self-guided tour option also stood out to prospects.

"Amenities are great, the downtown view is beautiful to watch, overall a very nice and quiet neighborhood close to many restaurants and shopping." (5 stars)

Amenity-rich living

From the Sky Lounge to the pet spa, the shared spaces are a frequent source of praise. Residents especially appreciate the fitness options, co-working space, and smart-home conveniences like the Nest thermostats.

Critical Revl Heights reviews

Not every experience has been positive. The lower-rated reviews cluster around four themes.

Maintenance follow-up

Some residents reported delays or dismissive responses to repair requests, and one said their unit was not cleaned well before move-in.

"The sink didn't work properly and was never truly fixed. Management would delete maintenance requests." (1 star)

Garage security and vehicle theft

Stolen wheels and break-ins in the garage are the biggest frustration in recent reviews.

"Less than two weeks after we moved in, my tires and rims were stolen. Management just said 'things happen.'" (1 star)

"There have been wheels stolen from cars... we had security for a month or so, then never again." (2 stars)

Strict guest towing

Guest parking runs through a VPP digital pass system, and several residents describe it as too strict: if a pass lapses even briefly, cars can be towed quickly.

"Guest parking sucks — only one guest can register per day, and you can't register another car until the 24 hours has passed." (2 stars)

Move-out billing and pricing

A few reviewers said deposits were withheld or charges were unclear, and one noted that the quoted price for a unit was higher than what was listed online.

"Pricing online was way lower than the actual quote given for the same unit. That's misleading." (4 stars)

Pros and cons of Revl Heights

ProsCons
Modern, stylish apartments with 10-foot ceilingsReports of slow maintenance follow-up
Extensive amenities, including a Sky Lounge and pet spaSecurity concerns in the parking garage
Pet-friendly with a dog parkStrict towing for guest vehicles
Fast, professional leasing teamSome move-out billing disputes
Quiet location near downtownOnline pricing may not match the quote

Questions to ask before you sign at Revl Heights

Reviews are a snapshot, so use them to shape your tour rather than make the decision for you. Based on the themes above, we would ask the leasing office:

  1. What security measures are currently in place in the garage, and has anything changed recently?
  2. How exactly does the VPP guest pass work, how long does a pass last, and how many guests can be registered per day?
  3. What is the typical turnaround on maintenance requests, and how can you track them?
  4. Is the price quoted in writing the same as what is listed online, and which fees (parking, EV charging, pet rent) are added monthly?
  5. What does the move-out inspection cover, and can you do a walk-through together?

It is also worth touring in the evening to see the garage and guest parking when most residents are home.

Is Revl Heights a good fit for you?

Revl Heights stands out as a well-designed, amenity-rich property in one of Houston's most desirable neighborhoods. If your priorities are modern finishes, smart-home features, in-unit laundry, and great shared spaces, it deserves a spot on your tour list. If garage security, quick maintenance, and flexible guest parking are deal-breakers, confirm how management has addressed those issues before you sign, or compare it with other options near downtown Houston.

You can book a tour or view available units on Revl Heights' official website.

Frequently asked questions

What is the rent at Revl Heights?

At the time of writing, rents ranged from $1,463 to $2,804 per month, depending on floor plan. Units range from 648 to 1,452 sq ft. Prices change often, so confirm current rates with the leasing office.

Is Revl Heights pet-friendly?

Yes. Cats and dogs are allowed, up to 2 pets per unit, with a $400 non-refundable pet fee and $25/month pet rent. The property also has a dog park and pet spa.

Does Revl Heights have secure parking?

Assigned garage parking is available for $40/month, and the community has controlled-access gates and video surveillance. However, some residents have reported vehicle thefts in the garage, so ask about current security measures when you tour.

How does guest parking work at Revl Heights?

Allure Hermann Park reviews paint a picture of a polished luxury high-rise with standout staff and views, held back mainly by elevator and maintenance complaints. The 29-story tower at 5927 Almeda Road, Houston, TX 77004 holds a 4.4-star Google rating at the time of writing, and sits minutes from the Texas Medical Center and Hermann Park.

Below, we break down what residents love, what they complain about, and what the building offers so you can decide whether it belongs on your tour list.

Allure Hermann Park at a Glance

Allure Hermann Park at Med Center was built in 2009 and has 396 units across 29 stories. It is a natural fit for medical professionals, students, and anyone who wants a short commute to the Medical Center, Hermann Park, or the Museum District.

What Residents Love About Allure Hermann Park

Friendly, standout staff

The most consistent theme in positive reviews is the team. Names like Gerry, Braxton, Rachel, and Russel come up again and again, with residents describing service that goes above and beyond.

“The staff is always helpful and responsive, especially Braxton… the valet staff were super helpful.” — Tache Antoine, 5 stars

“Gerry Quiroz, the concierge, is a bright light… she has been our personal cheerleader throughout my husband’s cancer treatments.” — Julie Countess, 5 stars

If personal service matters to you, the building’s 24/7 concierge and doorman are a real draw. Compare it with other Houston apartments with concierge services to see how it stacks up.

Luxury amenities that get used

Reviewers describe the community as a true luxury experience, with a resort-style pool, a lap pool, a fitness center, a clubhouse, valet service, and a shuttle to the Medical Center.

“The gym is never crowded… feels like a luxury escape.” — Tache Antoine, 5 stars

“The amenities are amazing… including a full gym, lap pool, and 24/7 concierge.” — Arav Singhal, 5 stars

Easy leasing and move-in

Several residents say signing a lease was smooth and low-pressure, which set a good tone from day one.

“Rachel was extremely informative and patient… I changed my mind on units three times and she remained pleasant.” — Tracy Richard, 5 stars

Skyline views and a quiet atmosphere

Floor-to-ceiling windows, balconies with sunset views, and high-floor vantage points over the Houston skyline are favorite features. Residents also mention the quiet gym, clean lobbies, and a serene pool area.

“The highlight of every day is coming home and seeing the beautiful sunsets through my floor-to-ceiling windows.” — Hannah Denman, 5 stars

Common Complaints in Allure Hermann Park Reviews

Not every review is glowing. The critical feedback clusters around a few recurring issues.

Elevator reliability

This is the most frequently mentioned problem. In a 29-story tower, residents report breakdowns, long waits, and stretches with only some of the four elevators running.

“All 4 elevators would work for a few months… but then we’d be left with 2 running elevators for weeks.” — Arav Singhal, 5 stars

“The elevators are often dirty and out of service… rare for all four to be operational at the same time.” — Andrea Fontova, 5 stars

Maintenance delays and water damage

One resident described a run of serious problems, from a washer that was out for weeks to a ceiling leak and water overflowing into the bathroom and bedroom.

“Water overflowed into my bathroom and bedroom… I had to stay in a hotel.” — Zehra Raza, 1 star

Others report prompt service for minor issues, so maintenance experiences appear mixed rather than uniformly poor.

Cleanliness, odors, and packages

A few reviewers mention dirty elevators and hallways they attribute to pets, smoke odors noticeable inside units, and packages going missing without proper control.

“Packages left unattended are frequently taken without permission… unacceptable that there is no proper control.” — Andrea Fontova, 5 stars

Occasional leasing office friction

Most leasing feedback is positive, but one reviewer reported poor communication, including a name repeatedly misspelled on documents.

The tradeoffs are real, though. Before signing, ask management how they handle elevator outages, how quickly larger repairs are typically completed, and how packages are secured. Tour at a busy time of day, such as the morning rush, to see how the elevators perform. Reading 4001 Midtown reviews before you tour? Here's the short version: residents consistently praise the leasing and management team, the amenities, and the Midtown location, while the most common complaints involve hallway cleanliness, slow fixes on bigger maintenance issues, and garage security. The community sits at 4001 Fannin St, Houston, TX 77004 and held a 4.2-star rating on Google at the time of writing.

Below, we break down what residents love, what they'd change, and what you actually get for your rent, so you can walk into your tour with the right questions.

4001 Midtown at a Glance

DetailWhat the listing and reviews show

What Residents Love About 4001 Midtown

The positive 4001 Midtown reviews follow a few clear themes: people, amenities, location, and community.

A leasing and management team residents name personally

Staff get more praise than anything else. Reviewers call out Chelsea, Aimee, Shanell, and others by name for being friendly, responsive, and attentive. Several residents credit the manager with improving the overall feel of the property.

"Aimee has completely transformed the atmosphere of the property. Everything else feels more organized, cleaner and much more community oriented. She goes above and beyond!"

"I had the pleasure of working with Shanell during my apartment search and she was PHENOMENAL! The tour was well worth seeing the different unit styles."

Upscale amenities and updated interiors

The resort-style pool, fitness center, clubhouse, and concierge coffee bar come up again and again. Community amenities include:

  • Resort-style pool and spa
  • 24-hour fitness center
  • BBQ and courtyard areas
  • Concierge coffee bar
  • Clubhouse
  • Gated garage and on-site parking (ask the leasing office for parking details)
  • Pet-friendly spaces

Inside the apartments, residents mention wood flooring, vaulted ceilings, and large closets. Select units add den layouts, fireplaces, and private balconies or patios. If a den or fireplace matters to you, ask which specific floor plans include them, since they aren't standard in every unit.

A central Midtown location

Living in Midtown puts you close to restaurants, museums, parks, and nightlife, with quick access to downtown Houston and public transit. Reviewers like how much is nearby, and one was surprised by how quiet it feels for the area.

"Honestly a very quiet neighborhood surprisingly for Midtown. The front staff is always attentive. Aimee the manager will always be there for her tenants. I've been here for about a year now and always felt safe."

"Gated garage with access control, nice neighbors, locker room for packages… Proximity to downtown is great."

A real sense of community

Residents mention regular events that make it easy to meet neighbors. For anyone new to Houston, that kind of programming can make a big building feel smaller.

"The community does a great job of making tenants feel welcome with all the fun events they host. There's always something going on that makes it easy to meet neighbors."

Pet-friendly policies

The pet policy is generous for an urban community: up to two pets per apartment, each up to 99 lbs. Expect a $400 one-time fee plus $25 per month per pet, and aggressive breeds are restricted. If you're comparing options, our pet-friendly Houston apartments search makes it easy to line up policies side by side.

Common Complaints in 4001 Midtown Reviews

Most reviews are positive, but a few concerns repeat often enough to take seriously.

Hallway and common-area cleanliness

Several reviewers say hallways and garage entries aren't always clean and could use a refresh or deeper clean.

"A simple refresh or deeper clean would make the whole building feel even nicer."

Maintenance on bigger problems

Some residents report slow resolution on serious issues like AC problems and water leaks. One reviewer described an AC leak that went unresolved for weeks, and another said balcony flooding took more than a week to fix and led to an $800 charge for carpet damage.

"Balcony flooding damaged our carpet… it took them more than a week to fix it, and then we got charged $800 for the damage."

Fees and portal mix-ups

A few residents felt surprised by extra service fees, and one said a renters insurance fee stayed on their portal even after both roommates submitted proof of coverage. Another reviewer noted the fees are explained at lease signing.

"A little bit of 'hidden' fees from services they provide — but they explain all of these when you sign the contract."

Garage security

Opinions are split here. Some residents say they've always felt safe, while one reported three large car break-ins between February and June 2025 and said tailgating is common and gates are sometimes left open.

Pros and Cons of Living at 4001 Midtown

ProsCons
Staff praised by name, especially the managerHallways and garage entries need better upkeep

Questions to Ask on Your 4001 Midtown Tour

  1. What's the typical turnaround on urgent requests like AC or leaks, and is there after-hours maintenance?
  2. Which monthly service fees are required, and how do I get the renters insurance fee removed once I provide proof?
  3. What security measures are in place in the garage, and have any been added recently?
  4. Which floor plans include a den, fireplace, or balcony?
  5. How is parking assigned, and what does it cost?

It also helps to walk the hallways and garage yourself, ideally in the evening, so you see the property the way residents do.

Is 4001 Midtown Worth It?

With a 4.2-star Google rating at the time of writing, 4001 Midtown earns its reputation for friendly, professional staff, a prime Midtown location, quality amenities, and an active resident community. If those are your priorities, it deserves a spot on your tour list.

Just go in with eyes open on hallway upkeep, maintenance response, and garage security. Clarify every fee up front and keep a written record of maintenance requests, and you'll be in a good position to decide.

content:
Haverstock Hills Apartments reviews paint a tough picture: at the time of writing, the community at 5619 Aldine Bender Rd in the Aldine/Greenspoint area held a 2.3-star Google rating, with residents repeatedly flagging maintenance delays, safety concerns, and an unresponsive leasing office. Below, we break down what renters actually say so you can decide whether to tour or keep looking.

Disclaimer: This summary is based on publicly available Google reviews of Haverstock Hills Apartments. The 2.3-star rating reflects the score at the time of writing and may change. Summaries are our interpretation of resident feedback, and your experience may differ.

Haverstock Hills at a Glance

DetailWhat reviews show
Address5619 Aldine Bender Rd, Houston, TX 77032
AreaAldine / Greenspoint, North Houston
Google rating2.3 stars (at the time of writing)
Most common complaintsSlow maintenance, safety, leasing office communication, move-in delays
Most common praiseA few older reviews describe a quiet stay; recent praise is rare

The Overall Tone of Haverstock Hills Reviews

Search for Haverstock Hills Apartments reviews and the pattern is hard to miss. No community is perfect, but here the same four issues come up again and again: maintenance that doesn’t get done, serious safety worries, an unreliable leasing process, and poor communication from the office.

That doesn’t mean every experience is bad. Positive feedback exists, but it is rare and often several years old.

Maintenance and Repairs: The Most Repeated Complaint

A large share of reviews describe long delays on critical repairs, especially:

  • Air conditioning failures during the summer
  • Plumbing and garbage disposal problems
  • Electrical outlets that don’t work
  • Unfinished or damaged flooring

Several residents said their AC went out in the summer and stayed out despite repeated calls and service requests. In Houston heat and humidity, that’s more than an inconvenience, and some tenants raised health concerns about prolonged heat inside their units.

Others reported moving into apartments with incomplete repairs, including unfinished floors, missing or broken appliances, and dead outlets, and said maintenance never came back to finish the work even after months of follow-up.

Leasing Office and Management Communication

Dozens of reviews describe the leasing office as disorganized and hard to reach. Common themes include:

  • Unanswered phone calls, pushing residents to visit the office in person for basic questions
  • Waiting hours to speak with someone, then getting confusion or indifference
  • A general feeling of being ignored or mistreated by the people managing the property

Move-In Delays and Broken Promises

The move-in process draws some of the heaviest criticism. Reviewers describe paying deposits and receiving move-in dates, only to see those dates pushed back repeatedly, sometimes with little or no notice. Some were left waiting weeks, or even months, with no apartment number assigned and no progress updates.

Others said they were promised finished units but arrived to find repairs still underway or appliances missing. Tenants recall being told “your unit will be ready in two weeks” and then calling again and again without answers. A few said the team blamed broken windows or pending repairs for the delays but never followed up consistently.

Safety: A Major Concern in Recent Reviews

Safety should be near the top of any renter’s checklist, and this is where Haverstock Hills reviews are most alarming. Residents have reported:

  • Frequent gunfire at night
  • Suspicious activity both inside and outside the gated areas
  • Fights and arguments near common areas
  • A general sense of fear walking to and from the property after dark

Multiple reviews reference tragic events, including the death of an elderly woman that reviewers allegedly tied to an air conditioner that wasn’t fixed during a heatwave. Others mention news stories about crime or violence connected to the complex. One reviewer who owns a nearby restaurant said they no longer deliver to Haverstock Hills, day or night, because of safety concerns.

Are There Any Positive Haverstock Hills Reviews?

In fairness, yes, a few. Most come from people who lived there years ago. One former tenant who lived in the back area near Lee Road between 2010 and 2012 said they had no major issues and that keeping to yourself and focusing on work made for a quiet stay. Even so, that reviewer left a one-star rating.

Newer reviews rarely praise the property, and many of the five-star ratings on Google are either older or have no written comments to judge them by.

Pros and Cons Based on Resident Feedback

Possible prosReported cons
Some older reviews describe a quiet experienceSlow or unfinished repairs, especially AC
Location and cost may appeal to some rentersFrequent safety and crime concerns
Hard-to-reach leasing office and long waits
Delayed move-in dates and incomplete units

How to Protect Yourself If You’re Considering Haverstock Hills

If you’re still weighing an application, take these steps first:

  1. Tour in person and ask to see the exact unit you would move into, not a model.
  2. Visit at different times of day, including evening, to get a feel for the grounds.
  3. Talk to current residents about maintenance response times and safety.
  4. Get your move-in date and unit number in writing before paying a deposit.
  5. Document everything, from emails to move-in condition photos.
  6. Compare other options nearby and read their reviews side by side.

Is Haverstock Hills Worth the Risk?

Based on the volume and consistency of feedback, Haverstock Hills Apartments reviews point to a community struggling with systemic problems, from management to day-to-day upkeep. Affordability and location may make it tempting, but the risks residents describe are hard to ignore. If prompt service, peace of mind, and a secure home matter to you, it’s worth continuing your search.

At the time of writing, Haverstock Hills Apartments held a 2.3-star Google rating, with most reviews citing management, safety, and maintenance problems.

Are maintenance requests handled quickly at Haverstock Hills?

Many residents report long delays, especially for air conditioning, and some say repairs went unresolved for weeks or longer.

Is Haverstock Hills Apartments safe?

Many reviews raise safety concerns, including reports of gunfire, suspicious activity, and crime on the property. One nearby restaurant owner said they no longer deliver there. Visit at night and ask the office about current security measures before deciding.

Do move-in dates match what’s promised?

Many reviewers say move-in dates were pushed back, sometimes for weeks, after they paid a deposit. Get your unit number and move-in date in writing.

Are any Haverstock Hills reviews positive?

A few, but most are older. Recent feedback is largely negative and highlights ongoing issues.

description: Prose Hardy Yards reviews: what residents love (finishes, pools, downtown access) and what worries them (security, upkeep). Read this before you tour.

content:
Prose Hardy Yards reviews paint a split picture. Residents like the modern finishes, the amenities, and the quick hop to downtown, but security, cleanliness, and management follow-through come up again and again. Here is a straight summary of what renters say, plus what to check on a tour so you can decide if it fits.

Address: 1550 Burnett St, Houston, TX 77009
Overall rating: 4.0 stars at the time of writing

Disclaimer: This summary is based on public resident reviews available at the time of writing. Opinions reflect the personal experiences of past and current residents, and the overall rating may change over time.

Prose Hardy Yards at a Glance

Prose Hardy Yards sits in the historic Hardy Yards area, built on the former Union Pacific rail yard just north of downtown Houston. It markets itself as luxury urban living, and on paper the package is strong.

CategoryWhat the community offers
Address1550 Burnett St, Houston, TX 77009
Rating4.0 stars (at the time of writing)
In-unit featuresStainless steel GE appliances, granite countertops, vinyl wood flooring, smart locks, in-unit washer and dryer
Select unitsCity views, large kitchen islands, custom built-in mudrooms
Community amenitiesTwo pools with outdoor grilling areas, large pet park, putting green, 24/7 fitness center, co-working spaces, EV charging
NearbyUH Downtown, Saint Arnold's Brewing, Daikin Ball Park, quick freeway access

What Residents Like About Prose Hardy Yards

Attractive Apartments and Finishes

Positive reviews often start with the units themselves: spacious layouts, vinyl wood flooring, stainless steel GE appliances, granite countertops, and in-unit washers and dryers. Some homes add expansive city views, large kitchen islands, and custom built-in mudrooms, which residents say make daily life easier.

Close to Downtown, Without Living in the Middle of It

Residents describe the location as the best of both worlds: close enough to downtown for work, dining, and entertainment, yet tucked away enough to feel like a retreat. Quick freeway access is a big plus for commuters.

Staff Members Residents Mention by Name

Charles gets credit for making out-of-state moves seamless, and Maria is recognized for keeping shared spaces fresh and well maintained. When individual staff members stand out in reviews, it usually means the front-line experience can be good.

Amenities You Will Actually Use

Two swimming pools with grilling areas, a large pet park, a putting green, a 24/7 fitness center, and co-working spaces get regular mentions. Remote workers in particular like having a place to work outside the apartment.

Long-Term Residents Who Stayed for Years

Several reviewers say they lived here for multiple years and found the community accommodating and the interiors pleasant, which is a useful counterweight to the complaints below.

Common Complaints in Prose Hardy Yards Reviews

Security and Gate Problems

Security is the most cited issue by a wide margin:

  • Gates that are often broken, letting trespassers in
  • Reports of car break-ins, bicycle thefts, and catalytic converter thefts
  • Limited or invisible security presence despite promises of a courtesy officer

Cleanliness in Shared Spaces

Despite the luxury branding, multiple reviews mention dirty hallways, pet waste left unattended, and infrequent power washing. Valet trash service, which is a paid amenity here, is described as inconsistent.

Maintenance and Construction Quality

Some residents point to cheap materials, thin walls, and units vulnerable to leaks and mold. A few say repairs after water damage were left unfinished for months.

Management Responsiveness

Individual staff members earn praise, but management as a whole is criticized for slow responses, little follow-up, and safety issues that went unaddressed.

Noise and Neighbor Behavior

Reviews mention loud pool parties at night, neighbors smoking indoors, and occasional conflicts that escalated to police calls.

Parking and Access

  • Non-residents parking in resident spaces, including EV charging spots
  • Covered parking is available at an additional cost, but residents say theft and vandalism have still happened

Prose Hardy Yards Pros and Cons

Pros residents mentionCons residents mention
Modern finishes, smart locks, in-unit laundryBroken gates and reported thefts
Two pools, 24/7 gym, pet park, putting greenDirty hallways and pet waste in common areas
Co-working spaces for remote workThin walls, leaks, and slow water-damage repairs
Fast access to downtown and freewaysSlow management follow-up
Helpful individual staff (Charles, Maria)Noise from late-night pool gatherings; parking misuse

Marketing Promises vs. Day-to-Day Living

Where the marketing delivers: the interiors (stainless appliances, granite, vinyl wood floors, smart locks), the community perks (two pools, 24/7 fitness, grilling areas, pet park), and the location near UH Downtown, Saint Arnold's, and the freeways.

Where residents see gaps: security (broken gates, thefts, little visible patrol), upkeep (unclean hallways, slow or superficial fixes for mold and water damage), and neighbor issues (late-night pool noise and indoor smoking). For some tenants the finishes and location outweigh the problems. For others, the gap between the brochure and daily reality decides whether they renew.

What to Check When You Tour Prose Hardy Yards

  1. Test the gates yourself, both pedestrian and vehicle, and ask how quickly repairs are made when one breaks.
  2. Ask whether there is a courtesy officer or patrol, what hours they work, and how incidents are reported to residents.
  3. Ask the cost of covered parking and how resident and EV spaces are enforced.
  4. Walk the hallways and pet areas at different times of day, not just on the leasing route.
  5. Ask how often the valet trash runs and what happens when a pickup is missed.
  6. If a unit has had water damage, ask what was repaired and get any promised work in writing.
  7. If you are a light sleeper, ask for a unit away from the pool deck.

Bringing a pet? The pet park is a plus, but compare a few pet-friendly Houston apartments nearby before you sign.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is Prose Hardy Yards located?

Prose Hardy Yards is at 1550 Burnett St, Houston, TX 77009, near downtown Houston and close to UH Downtown and Saint Arnold's Brewing.

What amenities does Prose Hardy Yards offer?

The community has two pools with grilling areas, a 24/7 fitness center, co-working spaces, a large pet park with agility equipment, a putting green, and EV charging stations. Units include stainless steel appliances, granite countertops, smart locks, and in-unit laundry.

What are the most common complaints in Prose Hardy Yards reviews?

Security issues such as broken gates and theft, cleanliness of shared areas, maintenance quality after leaks, and inconsistent management responsiveness are the top complaints.

Is Prose Hardy Yards pet-friendly?

Yes. It allows pets and has a large pet park, though some residents say other owners do not always clean up after their animals.

Is Prose Hardy Yards a good choice for downtown commuters?

The location offers quick access to downtown and major freeways, which commuters like. Weigh that against the security concerns raised in reviews and ask about current measures on your tour.

Is Prose Hardy Yards Right for You?

title: Heights on Katy Reviews: What Renters Really Say

description: Heights on Katy reviews: great location and drive-up garage, but break-ins, slow repairs, and a $125 amenity fee. Know what to ask before you sign.
excerpt: Thinking of moving to the Washington Corridor in Houston? Before you commit, it’s worth digging into Heights on Katy reviews to see what renters are really saying. While the community markets itself as a modern, upscale haven with resort-style amenities and trendy finishes, the lived experience appears to be a mixed bag. Some residents rave […]
content:
Heights on Katy reviews are sharply divided. Residents like the central Washington Corridor location, the drive-up parking garage, and reasonable pet fees, but many others report car break-ins, broken gates, slow maintenance, and units that didn't match the model they toured. At the time of publication, the community at 7105 Old Katy Rd held a 3.6-star rating.

Here's what renters are actually saying, what the property advertises, and how to protect yourself if you're considering a lease.

Heights on Katy overview

Heights on Katy markets itself as a modern, upscale community with resort-style amenities and trendy finishes. Its location near key highways and downtown Houston is a big part of the appeal, and it sits close to the Houston Heights and Washington Corridor.

DetailWhat the community lists
Address7105 Old Katy Rd, Houston, TX 77024
Rating3.6 stars (at the time of publication)
Amenity fee$125 per month, per resident reviews
Advertised amenities2 pools, basketball court, bark park, sand volleyball, 24-hour fitness center, clubhouse, onsite storage, package lockers, central parking garage
In-home features (select units)Quartz or granite countertops, custom tile backsplashes, stainless-steel appliances, large walk-in closets, faux-wood plank flooring

What renters like about Heights on Katy

Helpful leasing staff at move-in

Many residents describe a positive move-in experience and name specific staff, such as leasing agent Dana and front desk team member Jesse. One new tenant said Dana sent videos of available units during their workday, and staff helped them get set up with the package lockers.

"Anything I have needed the staff has been helpful. I really felt welcomed."

Location and the drive-up garage

Location is the most consistent positive. Residents also love the central parking garage that lets them drive up to their own floor instead of hauling groceries across a lot.

"The price and location are great. I really enjoy the center garage that lets you drive up to your floor."

Reasonable pet fees

Compared with other Houston communities, Heights on Katy earns credit for relatively low pet rent and deposits.

"The pet rent and deposit are much better here than other locations."

Storage, pools, and a basic gym

Some residents appreciated the pricing on onsite storage and access to the courtyard seating areas and pools when they were open. The fitness center covers the basics, with cardio equipment, dumbbells, and machines, though serious lifters may find it limited.

Modern finishes in select units

Upgraded homes feature quartz or granite countertops, tile backsplashes, stainless appliances, and walk-in closets. Expect to pay more for those upgrades.

"You do pay a little extra for units to have updated appliances like stainless steel fridge."

For residents who find the amenities in working order, the lifestyle can be a real draw:

"This is the kind of community that molds your life into something extraordinary, even in the little moments."

Common complaints in Heights on Katy reviews

While some reviewers enjoyed parts of the community, the majority of reviews raised serious concerns.

Security and car break-ins

This was the most frequent and severe complaint. Residents report car break-ins, stolen tools and tires, and vehicle theft from both the garage and open parking. Several say the gates were broken for months, and some claim management didn't alert residents after incidents.

"8 vehicles were broken into last week and a set of tires were taken from another vehicle."

"There's no security guard, no fire watch, and no accountability."

Units that didn't match the model

Several renters said they toured upgraded model units, then moved into unrenovated, outdated, or dirty apartments.

"We clarified multiple times that our apartment would look exactly like the model… Today, we go to move in and it is a completely different style and filthy."

Maintenance delays

Residents describe leaky ceilings, holes in walls left for months, A/C outages, broken washers, and faulty key fobs.

"It's been 8 months since they took out drywall for a leak. The hole is still there."

"My A/C broke and it took forever to fix it in the Houston heat."

Sanitation and pests

Some reviews mention maggot and fly infestations, dog waste, and trash left out for days.

"There was a maggot infestation that broke out down the hallway… the maggots made their way inside my apartment."

Paying for amenities that don't work

Residents say they pay a $125 monthly amenities fee while pools, grills, and gym equipment are often broken or closed.

"Both pools are closed, 3 of 4 grills are broken, valet trash service is awful. Still charged amenities fees for all the non-working amenities."

Management turnover

Several reviews mention frequent management changes, poor communication, and little follow-through.

"Office staff is constantly changing and hard to reach. The manager is always 'busy' or out."

Pros and cons at a glance

ProsCons
Central location near highways and downtownFrequent car break-ins and broken gates
Drive-up parking garageMove-in units not matching models
Lower pet rent and depositsLong maintenance delays
Helpful individual leasing staff$125 amenity fee for amenities often closed
Modern finishes in select unitsManagement turnover and poor communication

How to lease smart at Heights on Katy

Heights on Katy has real strengths, but the volume of troubling reviews means you should go in with eyes open:

  • Tour the exact unit you'll be renting, not just the model.
  • Get everything in writing, including finishes, appliances, and any promised repairs.
  • Ask which amenities are open right now and what the $125 fee covers.
  • Ask how residents are notified about security incidents and whether the gates are working.
  • Consider renter's insurance that covers vehicle contents.

If the Washington Corridor appeals to you, compare nearby options in our Rice Military apartments guide, or read our Heights West End reviews for another take on the area.

Frequently asked questions

What amenities does Heights on Katy offer?

The community advertises two resort-style pools, a 24-hour fitness center, basketball and sand volleyball courts, a clubhouse, and a bark park. Many reviewers say these amenities are often broken or closed.

Are the apartments updated?

Select homes have stainless appliances, quartz or granite countertops, and tile backsplashes. Several reviewers say they were promised updated units but received outdated ones, so confirm your specific unit in writing.

Is Heights on Katy safe?

Security is the top concern in reviews, with frequent mentions of car break-ins, stolen items, and broken gates. Visit at night and ask management about current security measures.

Is Heights on Katy pet friendly?

Yes, and residents say its pet rent and deposits compare favorably to other Houston communities. You can also browse pet-friendly Houston apartments to compare.

How is maintenance at Heights on Katy?

Many renters report slow responses and issues left unresolved for months, including leaks and broken appliances.

Disclaimer: This article summarizes public reviews for Heights on Katy at 7105 Old Katy Rd, Houston, TX 77024. Reviews reflect individual opinions, and the 3.6 rating was accurate at the time of publication. Always do your own research and visit in person before signing a lease.

title: Summit at Renaissance Park Reviews: Pros, Cons and Tips
seo_title: Summit at Renaissance Park Reviews: Pros & Cons
description: Summit at Renaissance Park reviews, summarized: upscale finishes and praised leasing tours, plus warnings about income rules, fees, and management.
excerpt: When searching for the right home, diving into Summit at Renaissance Park reviews offers invaluable insight into the reality behind the glossy marketing. Located at 12121 Greenspoint Dr in Houston, TX, this apartment complex promises luxury living on an affordable scale, but does it deliver? With an overall Google rating of 4.2 stars, this community […]
content:
Summit at Renaissance Park reviews tell a split story: renters praise the modern finishes, amenities, and leasing tours, while applicants and residents warn about confusing income qualification, non-refundable fees, and management follow-through. The community sits at 12121 Greenspoint Dr in Houston, TX and held an overall Google rating of 4.2 stars at the time of writing.

Here is what the property offers, what people like, what they complain about, and how to protect yourself if you apply.

Property Overview

Summit at Renaissance Park is a recently built, income-qualified community designed to offer affordable housing with upscale finishes. Its marketing tagline sums up the pitch: "Live carefree every day. At Summit at Renaissance Park, coming home feels like you're on vacation."

Because it is income-restricted, it is worth understanding how these programs work before you apply. Our guide to tax credit apartments in Houston explains the basics, and you can also browse income-restricted apartments across the city.

In-unit features

  • Washer and dryer
  • Granite countertops
  • Stainless steel appliances
  • Island kitchen
  • Tub/shower, oven, range, and refrigerator

Community amenities

  • Controlled access
  • EV charging stations
  • Fitness center
  • Pool, sundeck, and playground
  • Clubhouse, lounge, and business center
  • Package service and 24-hour access
  • Picnic area and grill
  • Public transportation access
  • Planned social activities

What is nearby

Nearby spots include Imperial Hot Chicken, Uncle Tong's, and Mr. Soysauce for food; Walmart Supercenter, Ross, and the Greens CrossRoads shopping center for errands; and Flip N' Fun Trampoline Park and AMC theaters for entertainment.

What Renters Like

Leasing tours with Lee Charles

The single most praised name in the reviews is Lee Charles. Visitors describe him as courteous, knowledgeable, and attentive, with one reviewer saying he made the tour relaxed and pressure-free. Several noted his transparency about availability and pricing.

High-end finishes in affordable housing

Reviewers call out the granite countertops, sleek appliances, and island kitchens. The impression many left with was of upscale living at an affordable rate, and in-unit laundry is a perk many renters specifically look for (see more Houston apartments with a washer and dryer).

Resort-style amenities

The fitness center, pool, and picnic areas came up positively. Reviews did not go deep on every amenity, but their presence adds value.

Convenient location

Easy access to Greens CrossRoads, daily essentials, and public transportation is seen as a plus.

What Renters Warn About

Safety and cleanliness

One resident reported regular drug use on the property despite its non-smoking designation, describing a persistent marijuana smell in units and shared spaces and raising concerns about enforcement.

Pest problems

A resident described a red ant infestation that remained unresolved despite their own efforts and multiple reports to management.

Inconsistent application and income rules

This is the biggest theme. One reviewer was told they qualified for a three-bedroom, then learned weeks later they only qualified for a one-bedroom. Another was denied despite meeting the monthly income requirement because of unclear annual income thresholds. Several reviewers, including veterans and low-income earners, felt the rules were contradictory and poorly explained.

Non-refundable fees

Reviewers were unhappy that application and deposit fees are non-refundable. One renter described paying nearly $400 without securing a unit.

Customer service and communication

One prospective tenant reported overhearing the leasing manager tell staff to prioritize lease signings over move-ins to "get numbers up." Another found that management's responses to online reviews were automated and impersonal. Some reviews also mentioned that only a few units were fully finished and ready to rent at the time.

Pros and Cons at a Glance

ProsCons
Granite counters, stainless appliances, island kitchensConfusing, inconsistent income qualification
In-unit washer and dryerNon-refundable application and deposit fees
Pool, fitness center, EV charging, business centerReports of drug use and pest issues
Highly praised leasing agent (Lee Charles)Management communication and follow-through
Close to shopping, dining, and transitLimited move-in-ready units reported

How to Apply Smart at Summit at Renaissance Park

The leasing team's strong reviews suggest that many complaints come down to communication. If you are interested, protect your time and money:

  • Take a thorough tour, and ask for Lee Charles if he is available.
  • Request the income limits for each unit size in writing before you pay anything.
  • Clarify exactly which fees are refundable and under what conditions.
  • Confirm that the specific unit you want is finished and move-in ready.
  • Speak with current residents, if possible, about day-to-day operations.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Summit at Renaissance Park income-restricted?

Yes. It is an income-qualified community, and several renters reported that the qualification process was confusing, with unclear thresholds for different unit sizes. Get the limits in writing before applying.

Is the application fee refundable?

No. Multiple reviewers were frustrated by non-refundable application and deposit fees, especially after being denied.

What features come in the apartments?

Units include a washer and dryer, granite countertops, stainless steel appliances, and an island kitchen.

Is the community safe and clean?

Experiences vary. Some felt the property looked clean and secure, while others reported drug use and pest issues. Visit at different times of day to judge for yourself.

How is management rated?

Reviews are mixed. Lee Charles is consistently praised, while others cite disorganization and poor communication from management.

Explore Your Options

title: Aliso Briar Forest Reviews: What Residents Really Say

description: Aliso Briar Forest reviews, summarized: residents love the lake, amenities and staff but flag car break-ins, towing and guest parking. See the full picture.
excerpt: Reading Aliso Briar Forest reviews can give you valuable insight before signing a lease at this popular Houston apartment complex. Located in the heart of the energy corridor at 14698 Briar Forest Dr, Aliso Briar Forest markets itself as a serene escape with resort-style amenities and a strong sense of community. From a tranquil on-site […]
content:
Aliso Briar Forest reviews are split: many residents love the lake setting, resort-style amenities and named staff members, while a vocal group reports car break-ins, aggressive towing and communication gaps. The community at 14698 Briar Forest Dr in the Energy Corridor held a 3.9-star overall Google rating at the time of writing.

We read through the Google reviews to pull out the praise and concerns that come up again and again, so you can decide whether Aliso Briar Forest fits what you need.

Aliso Briar Forest at a glance

DetailWhat we found
Address14698 Briar Forest Dr, Houston (Energy Corridor)
Google rating3.9 stars at the time of writing
Standout amenitiesOn-site lake with fountains and jogging paths, pool with sunshelf, 24-hour fitness center
PetsPet-friendly with pet park and waste stations; breed restrictions and fees apply
LeasesFlexible terms, including short-term options
Top complaintsCar break-ins and vandalism, guest parking and towing

What residents love about Aliso Briar Forest

Many residents describe a tranquil setting and genuinely helpful staff.

A scenic, resort-style setting

The most praised feature is the peaceful environment. The on-site lake with water fountains and jogging paths sets the tone, and the community adds:

  • Resort-style swimming pool with sunshelf
  • Clubhouse and game room
  • 24-hour fitness center
  • Volleyball court
  • Business center
  • BBQ and picnic area

Pet-friendly with secure package handling

Dog owners appreciate the on-site pet park and pet waste stations. A secure package concierge system keeps deliveries safe and accessible, and multiple reviewers called it out as a plus.

Staff residents mention by name

Reviewers frequently credit leasing and maintenance staff including Luke, Mariah, Cori, Yeni, Andy and Ricardo for their responsiveness and professionalism. One resident relocating from Florida said Luke made the move seamless and gave them peace of mind during a major transition.

Interior features that impress

Residents like the bamboo wood flooring, stainless steel appliances, walk-in closets and private patios or balconies. High ceilings, spacious pantries and in-unit washers and dryers round out the list.

Convenient, flexible living

Online rent payments, online service requests and flexible lease terms make day-to-day life easier, especially for renters in transition.

Common complaints in Aliso Briar Forest reviews

Despite those strengths, a significant number of reviewers raised issues that affected their comfort and sense of safety.

Car break-ins and vandalism

Multiple 1-star reviews describe car break-ins, vandalism and even cars left on bricks after wheel thefts. Some reviewers said incidents happened repeatedly and felt management had not done enough to improve security.

Guest parking and towing

Guest parking is a major pain point. Reviewers criticized the QR code registration system, limited guest spaces and aggressive towing. One new resident said they were towed on their very first day and described the setup as predatory.

Questions about incentivized reviews

A few reviewers suspect some 5-star reviews were influenced by incentives, and suggested waiting until you have actually lived somewhere before reviewing it.

Communication and transparency

Some residents cited poor communication about fees and emergencies. One reviewer reported power outages after Hurricane Beryl and criticized the lack of updates or compensation.

Declining experience over time

A few residents said things got worse the longer they stayed, pointing to more noise, lax pet waste cleanup and slower maintenance responses.

Pros and cons summary

ProsCons
Lake, fountains and jogging pathsRepeated reports of car break-ins and wheel theft
Pool with sunshelf, 24-hour gym, game roomLimited guest parking and strict towing
Pet park and pet waste stationsGaps in communication about fees and outages
Praised leasing and maintenance staffSome say conditions declined over time
In-unit washer and dryer, high ceilings, walk-in closetsQuestions about incentivized 5-star reviews

Tips before you lease at Aliso Briar Forest

  • Ask where your assigned or nearest parking is and how well it is lit and covered by cameras.
  • Have guests test the QR code registration during your tour so you understand how it works.
  • Get the towing policy in writing, including move-in day rules.
  • Ask how the office communicates during outages and storms.
  • Read recent reviews from long-term residents, not just new move-ins.

Want similar features elsewhere? Compare Houston apartments with a washer and dryer or pet-friendly apartments on our map.

Frequently asked questions

What amenities does Aliso Briar Forest offer?

Amenities include a pool with sunshelf, 24-hour fitness center, game room, on-site lake with jogging paths, pet park, BBQ and picnic areas, volleyball court, business center and a resident clubhouse.

Is Aliso Briar Forest pet-friendly?

Yes. There is a dedicated pet park and pet waste stations. Breed restrictions and additional fees apply, including a refundable deposit and monthly pet rent.

How secure is Aliso Briar Forest?

The property has a gated entry and some security measures, but several residents reported vehicle vandalism and felt security coverage was inadequate, particularly in less visible areas.

What is the guest parking policy?

Guests register through a QR code system, and unregistered vehicles risk being towed. Limited guest spaces are a common complaint.

Does Aliso Briar Forest offer short-term leases?

Yes, the community offers flexible lease terms, including short-term options.

Is Aliso Briar Forest right for you?

Aliso Briar Forest is a strong match for dog owners, nature lovers and anyone who wants resort-style amenities and well-liked staff. Weigh that against repeated concerns about vehicle security, parking and transparency. The 3.9-star rating suggests a generally favorable experience, but the polarized reviews show results vary.
