Quiet courtyard units and good insulationElevator and garage door problems
Quartz kitchens, washer/dryer in every unitDisputed move-out charges and admin fees
Pet-friendly with a dog walking areaNoise complaints not always addressed

Before You Lease at 88twenty

Tour in person, ideally at the time of day you’d be coming and going. Ask about current security measures, how move-out charges are calculated, whether the admin fee is refundable, and which buildings have finished common-area renovations. Take dated photos at move-in so you have a record later. Pet owners should also ask about breed restrictions and fees up front; our pet-friendly Houston apartments search can help you compare.

Frequently asked questions

What floor plans does 88twenty offer?

Studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom layouts, all open concept, with features like quartz countertops, stainless steel appliances, and wood-style flooring.

Is 88twenty pet friendly?

Yes. Residents may have up to two pets. Breed restrictions apply, there are pet fees, deposits, and monthly pet rent, and exotic pets aren’t allowed.

What amenities does 88twenty have?

A fitness center, outdoor pool, resident lounge with a pool table, dog walking area, gated garage parking, a parcel locker system, and resident events.

Where is 88twenty located?

At 8820 Westheimer Rd in the Uptown area of West Houston, near Piney Point Village and close to the Galleria, major highways, the Houston Zoo, and Memorial Park.

What are the most common complaints about 88twenty?

Noise from neighbors and dogs, inconsistent upkeep of common areas, safety incidents, and unclear move-out charges or admin fees.

Find Your Fit Near the Galleria

88twenty pairs upscale interiors with a well-liked staff, but weigh the safety and fee concerns carefully. To compare it with nearby options, search Houston apartments on our map or talk to a Houston Apartments locator. Our help is free, and you can get up to $500 back when you lease through us.

content:
Charleston at Fannin Station reviews are mostly positive: residents praise the upscale interiors, resort-style amenities, and a staff that many call the best part of living there. The complaints that do show up center on lease communication, a few slow repairs, and noise. We looked at ten Google reviews to show you both sides before you tour.

Address: 9779 Fannin Rail Way, Houston, TX 77045
Google rating: 4.5 stars at the time of writing

Disclaimer: This article is based on 10 Google reviews for Charleston at Fannin Station. Reviews reflect the personal experiences of individual renters and may not represent every tenant's experience. Always tour the property and speak directly with staff before making a rental decision.

Charleston at Fannin Station at a Glance

The community sits just off Fannin Rail Way, minutes from NRG Park, the Museum District, and the Texas Medical Center, with the Fannin Station METRORail stop close by.

CategoryDetails
Home typesOne- and two-bedroom apartments, penthouse suites, and stand-alone townhomes
InteriorsOversized kitchen islands, granite countertops, 42-inch soft-close cabinetry, subway tile backsplashes, 9- to 13-foot ceilings, oversized double-paned windows, walk-in closets with wood shelving, front-loading washers and dryers, warm or cool color schemes
AmenitiesResort-style pool with semi-private cabanas, two-level fitness center, yoga studio, billiard lounge, internet cafe, clubroom with fireplace, outdoor kitchen with gourmet grills, dog park
Services24-hour emergency maintenance, doorstep trash pickup, mobile concierge, key fob access, parcel lockers

What Residents Love About Charleston at Fannin Station

Design and Premium Interiors

Residents frequently describe the property as visually impressive and modern. Kitchens feature oversized islands, granite countertops, 42-inch soft-close cabinetry, and subway tile backsplashes. Tenants also call out the ceilings that reach up to 13 feet, natural light from oversized double-paned windows, walk-in closets with wood shelving, and front-loading washers and dryers.

Beyond standard apartments, the community offers penthouse suites and stand-alone townhomes. If you want more separation from neighbors, our guide to townhomes for rent in Houston covers more options.

Resort-Style Amenities That Deliver

The resort-style pool with semi-private cabanas and the two-level fitness center with Peloton, Precor, and free weights get the most mentions. A yoga studio, billiard lounge, internet cafe, and clubroom with a fireplace give residents places to unwind or socialize, and an outdoor kitchen with gourmet grills handles weekend cookouts.

Day-to-day conveniences matter too: 24-hour emergency maintenance, doorstep trash pickup, and a mobile concierge system all come up as reasons residents feel well looked after.

Standout Maintenance and Leasing Staff

The most consistent theme in positive reviews is the staff. Residents call out team members by name for going above and beyond. The property manager is recognized for her open-door policy and commitment to improving the community, and maintenance tech Miguel earns praise for prompt, professional service. For some tenants, the staff's helpfulness is what convinced them to renew.

What Residents Warn About

Communication and Lease Disputes

Some residents report miscommunication and poor follow-up around lease terminations, renewals, and billing. A few believed agreements had been made verbally or by email, only to face unexpected charges later. In sensitive situations, such as needing to move after a personal loss or storm damage, some felt their concerns were handled without empathy, and say solutions were offered only after they posted negative reviews.

Delays on Certain Repairs

Routine maintenance appears responsive, but some repairs took much longer. One resident reported going months without a working dishwasher despite repeated requests. Reviews suggest delays are more likely when a repair needs third-party involvement.

Noise, Trash, and Community Conduct

Several reviews mention thin walls, trash left in hallways, and rowdy pool parties. The property has key fob access and parcel lockers, but some residents want stricter enforcement around unauthorized guests and cleanliness. Fire alarms going off at odd hours and pet owners not cleaning up after their dogs were also mentioned.

Pros and Cons at a Glance

ProsCons
High ceilings, granite kitchens, big windowsLease and billing disputes for some residents
Two-level gym, yoga studio, pool cabanasLong waits on certain repairs, like appliances
Friendly, named-in-reviews staffThin walls and pool-party noise
Near NRG Park, Museum District, and the Medical CenterHallway trash and pet waste
Close to the Fannin Station METRORail stopFire alarms at odd hours

Who Charleston at Fannin Station Suits Best

  • Medical Center commuters who want rail access and a short trip to work. Compare it with other apartments near the Medical Center.
  • Amenity lovers who will actually use the gym, yoga studio, and pool.
  • Renters who want a townhome or penthouse option without leaving a managed community.

If you are sensitive to noise, ask for a unit away from the pool and request a look at a top-floor or end unit.

Frequently Asked Questions

What types of apartments are available at Charleston at Fannin Station?

One- and two-bedroom apartments, penthouse suites, and stand-alone townhomes, with warm or cool color schemes, granite countertops, oversized islands, and 9- to 13-foot ceilings.

Are the amenities as nice as advertised?

Many residents say yes, pointing to the resort-style pool with cabanas, two-level gym, yoga studio, billiard lounge, and outdoor kitchen.

How responsive is maintenance?

Maintenance is generally praised and most requests are handled promptly, though some repairs that require outside vendors have taken longer.

Is Charleston at Fannin Station pet-friendly?

Yes. It has an on-site dog park, though some residents mention other owners not picking up after their pets.

How do I avoid lease disputes here?

Get every agreement about renewals, early termination, or billing in writing, keep copies of emails, and confirm the final terms before you sign.

Is Charleston at Fannin Station the Right Fit?

With modern design, strong amenities, a 4.5-star Google rating, and quick access to the Medical Center and METRORail, Charleston at Fannin Station has a lot going for it. Go in with eyes open on lease communication, and put agreements in writing.

content:
Briarwood Apartments Houston reviews lean negative. A few tenants praise specific leasing staff, spacious layouts, and the Galleria-area location, but many more report mold, leaks, pests, a broken security gate, and surprise move-out charges. At the time of writing, the community at 2520 Winrock Blvd held a 3.0-star Google rating.

Below is an honest summary of what tenants say, plus a checklist to use if you're still considering a lease here.

About Briarwood Apartments

Briarwood Apartments markets itself as a charming community of 1-, 2-, and 3-bedroom apartments and townhomes near the Galleria. Management highlights its location near Briargrove Elementary and The Galleria for dining, shopping, and public transportation.

DetailWhat the community lists
Address2520 Winrock Blvd, Houston, TX 77057
Google rating3.0 stars (at the time of writing)
Floor plans1, 2, and 3 bedrooms, plus townhomes
AmenitiesFour swimming pools, tree-lined grounds, on-site laundry facilities
In-home featuresBuilt-in bookshelves, fireplaces, walk-in closets, private patios or balconies

The marketing paints a picturesque image. Tenant reviews suggest a more complicated reality.

What tenants like about Briarwood Apartments

Positive reviews are in the minority, but they do highlight a few real strengths:

  • Friendly staff: Tenants praised leasing office employees including Ms. Ermy, Jesus, and Christina for professionalism and warmth at move-in.
  • Smooth move-ins: One tenant said the office made the transition seamless.
  • Improving management: A recent tenant said response times improved and management became more professional after Jesus joined the office.
  • Community feel: A few residents said the complex can feel friendly and welcoming.
  • Spacious layouts: Some enjoy the larger kitchens and living spaces, private balconies, and fireplaces.

Common complaints in Briarwood Apartments reviews

Management and customer service

  • Many tenants describe management as unresponsive and unprofessional; some used words like "rude," "unhelpful," and "vindictive," alleging maintenance was withheld as retaliation.
  • The office is accused of ignoring calls and emails. One reviewer compared it to a "bad Tinder date."
  • A long-term tenant said they were treated poorly at move-out and overcharged for utilities and unexplained fees.

Maintenance and living conditions

  • Mold: Several tenants reported black mold that they say was painted over instead of fixed.
  • Leaks: Multiple complaints describe ongoing water leaks, some damaging belongings.
  • Pests: Rats, roaches, and even termites falling from walls were reported. One tenant said rats chewed through their kitchen.
  • Requests marked "completed": Tenants say the online portal closed out requests that were never resolved.
  • Aging appliances: Reports include refrigerators that don't stay cold, persistently leaking sinks, and appliances "painted over" instead of repaired.

Security

  • The security gate is described as constantly broken.
  • Residents reported vehicle theft and break-ins with little response from management.
  • Homeless individuals were reportedly sheltering in the laundry rooms.
  • One tenant described a police chase that ended inside the complex.

Move-out charges and billing

  • Former tenants reported unexpected deductions from their deposits.
  • One tenant was charged for extra months of utilities after moving out.
  • A recurring complaint involves renters' insurance charges despite tenants providing proof of coverage.

General upkeep

  • Dumpsters are reportedly always overflowing.
  • Stray cats roam the property and leave paw prints on cars.
  • One tenant said their garbage disposal pushed up food from neighboring units.
  • Broken cabinets and peeling paint were common complaints.
  • Some tenants criticized the immediate neighborhood, citing gang presence and frequent police activity.

Briarwood Apartments pros and cons

ProsCons
Location near The Galleria and Briargrove ElementaryReports of mold, leaks, and pests
Four pools and tree-lined groundsFrequently broken security gate and car break-ins
Spacious layouts with fireplaces and balconiesUnresponsive management, per many reviews
Some standout leasing staffUnexpected move-out and insurance charges

Checklist before you lease at Briarwood

Tour the exact unit

The model may look great, but reviews say actual units can differ. Look closely at walls, floors, and ceilings for water damage or mold. Test appliances, faucets, and lights. Photograph any existing damage before move-in.

Ask how maintenance works

Ask about typical response times, how emergencies are handled, and whether you'll get updates on requests. If you can, ask current residents how their repairs went.

Verify security

Check whether the gate and cameras work, and visit after dark to see how well parking areas and walkways are lit.

Get every fee in writing

Ask for a breakdown of deposits, admin fees, and utility billing. Read the lease's terms on cleaning fees and early termination, confirm how renters' insurance proof is recorded, and request a final walk-through before you move out.

If you love the area but want more options, our Galleria apartments guide covers communities nearby, and our Houston apartments with fireplaces roundup lists other places with that cozy feature.

Frequently asked questions

What amenities does Briarwood Apartments offer?

Four swimming pools, private patios or balconies, fireplaces, walk-in closets, and on-site laundry facilities, in a location near The Galleria.

Are there security concerns at Briarwood Apartments?

Yes. Multiple reviews mention a frequently broken entry gate, car thefts, and break-ins. Check security measures in person before committing.

How responsive is maintenance?

Experiences are mixed. Some residents note improvements, while others report long delays and unresolved leaks, mold, and pests.

Does Briarwood have townhomes?

Yes. The community offers townhomes alongside 1-, 2-, and 3-bedroom apartments.

What should I check before signing?

Inspect the actual unit, clarify all fees, and understand the lease terms around move-out charges and utility billing.

Briarwood may suit renters who put location and space ahead of maintenance and security, but go in prepared. Common Complaints About Allora Gosling

Noise from upstairs neighbors

"I get off at 10pm and have to park three or four buildings away from my apartment every single night." – 1 star

The building at 1617 Fannin St in downtown Houston held an overall Google rating of 2.7 stars at the time of writing.

We pulled together the most consistent themes from recent Google reviews, both good and bad, so you can decide whether Houston House is worth a tour.

Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available Google reviews at the time of writing. These are the personal opinions and experiences of residents and do not reflect the official stance of Houston House Apartments or its management.

Houston House Apartments at a glance

DetailWhat we found

Google rating2.7 stars at the time of writing

What residents like about Houston House Apartments

Despite the low rating, not every review is negative. A handful of residents found real value here.

A prime downtown location near the rail

The most frequently mentioned perk is location. The building is about a block from a Metro Rail station, which makes commuting to the Texas Medical Center and other parts of the city easy for renters who rely on transit.

“The property is one block away from a Metro Rail station so it is great for those that work in Med Center.” – 3 stars

If a rail commute to the medical center is your priority, our Medical Center apartments guide covers more options along the line.

Impressive skyline views

Several reviewers said the views from their terraces are genuinely beautiful.

“I like having central air/heat, a dishwasher and a great terrace view.” – 4 stars

Spacious living rooms

Some residents found the floor plans, especially living rooms, larger than expected for downtown, which helps if you entertain or work from home.

“The Floorplan I looked at had a large living room.” – 3 stars

Friendly staff, at times

Some renters described the front desk and maintenance team as friendly and responsive, with some requests handled promptly.

“The people that work in the office and the front desk are friendly and do their best to get things done.” – 4 stars

Major complaints in Houston House Apartments reviews

Based on recent reviews, the negative experiences far outweigh the positive, and many complaints repeat across multiple tenants.

Roach infestations

The single most common complaint is roaches. Multiple reviewers described severe infestations, and some said roaches persisted even though pest control charges appeared on their monthly bills.

“The ROACHES!!!!!! I cannot express enough how absolutely disgusting and miserable my partner and I are because of the roaches.” – 1 star

“This place is just straight up nasty from the infestation of roaches all the way down to the nasty conditions of the elevator hallways and parking garage.” – 1 star

Dirty common areas

Reviewers described elevators, hallways and the parking garage as filthy, with urine, vomit and trash left behind.

“The common areas are extremely dirty! The parking garage and elevator areas look as if they never had been cleaned before.” – 2 stars

“I’ve walked into pee and vomit-filled elevators.” – 1 star

Noise, parties and unruly neighbors

Several reviews mention loud neighbors, hallway skateboarding, fights and frequent party-style gatherings, with the 19th floor called out specifically.

“It feels like frat parties every other day in there.” – 1 star

“Young punks running up and down the hallway banging doors and riding skateboards screaming and yelling.” – 2 stars

Security and car break-ins

Residents reported frequent car break-ins in the garage and non-residents using amenities like the pool and basketball court. Reviewers noted that a Houston Police Department officer living on site rent-free had not provided much comfort.

“There were so many strangers that didn’t live in the actual apartment building coming in and out using the pool and basketball court.” – 1 star

“My car was broken into recently along with many others.” – 2 stars

Broken elevators and limited laundry

Reviewers complained about outdated amenities, elevators that stopped working, and a laundry room too small for the building.

“There is no washer and dryer in any unit except for one floorplan, and the laundromat they have on-site is very small.” – 3 stars

“There were so many times where I had to literally take the stairs from the 17th floor all the way down to the first floor due to the elevators not working!” – 1 star

Disorganized management

Reviewers cited missed appointments, ignored maintenance requests and confusing move-out policies that led to unexpected charges.

“Management here should be Q&A and audited!! By far the worst apartment experience I’ve ever had!” – 1 star

“They NEVER answer the phone.” – 1 star

Should you move into Houston House Apartments?

Reviewers describe Houston House as a budget-friendly downtown option, but one that comes at the cost of cleanliness, security and quiet. If location, views and a big living room come first, you may find value here. If you want a well-maintained, secure and quiet home, keep looking.

Before you sign a lease

  1. Tour in person and check the elevators, hallways and garage, not just the model unit.
  2. Ask about pest control history for the specific unit, and what the monthly pest fee covers.
  3. Ask which floor plan has a washer and dryer if in-unit laundry matters to you.
  4. Read the lease carefully, especially move-out policies and extra fees.
  5. Ask about garage security and how amenity access is controlled.

If in-unit laundry is a must, you can search Houston apartments with a washer and dryer instead.

Roach infestations, dirty common areas, car break-ins and security concerns, loud neighbors, broken elevators and unresponsive management.

Yes. Residents mention the central location, rail access, skyline views and spacious living rooms.

Only one floor plan has an in-unit washer and dryer, according to reviewers. There is a small on-site laundry room that residents say is often crowded.

Community and safety

Many reviewers describe Aris as a real community, thanks to regular resident events and a warm staff. They also highlight clean, well-kept common areas and say they feel safe in their downtown home.

What Residents Love About Westview Forest

A real sense of community

Residents often describe Westview Forest as welcoming and inclusive. Staff members Amanda, Andrea, and Christina are praised for being professional and responsive, and events like Halloween celebrations for kids and resident meetings with breakfast help neighbors get to know each other.

“The staff is super friendly, and the neighbors around us have shown what a community is. It’s a place where your opinion matters.”

Security that residents notice

The gated community has a staffed guardhouse around the clock, monitored cameras, and careful visitor vetting. Many tenants, especially those coming from less secure complexes, say it is a big reason they feel at home.

“The security is very good, and the staff in the guardhouse know my face, my car, and even my regular visitors. It feels like a haven amidst the surrounding area.”

Affordable rent and low utility bills

Budget-friendly rent is a recurring theme. Well-insulated apartments and white roofs help keep electricity costs down, and remodeled units get positive mentions.

“My first electric bill surprised me—it was less than half of what I expected. The rates are affordable, and the apartments are nicely remodeled.”

Genuinely pet-friendly

With no size restrictions, a maintained dog park with waste stations, and a dog wash station, Westview Forest is a good match for owners of larger dogs or multiple pets.

“Westview Forest was able to accept both my furry babies. I love that they’re so pet-friendly!”

Pools, laundry, and proactive maintenance

Three pools, on-site laundry, and hookups in select units cover the basics. Residents describe the maintenance team as quick and the grounds as clean.

“The maintenance team is excellent. They fix issues quickly, and the grounds are always clean,” one resident noted.

A convenient west Houston location

The property is close to Memorial City Mall, restaurants, bars, I-10, and Beltway 8. Memorial Hermann Hospital and a nearby fire station add peace of mind. Our Memorial City apartments guide covers more of the surrounding area.

Common Complaints in Westview Forest Apartments Reviews

Pests on the ground floor

Some ground-floor residents report mosquitoes and cockroaches. Staff respond when issues are reported, but it is a recurring frustration for a few tenants.

“The constant battle with mosquitoes and cockroaches is frustrating, but they do address it when I report it.”

Parking rules

Residents get parking stickers, reserved spots cost extra, and visitors need a pass or risk a fine. Some find guest parking limited and the pass system a hassle.

“Parking is fairly limited, and one-time passes are a hassle. I even received a fine for parking my company car in my reserved spot while my personal car was at the mechanic.”

No online rent payments

At the time of the reviews, rent was paid by money order rather than online, which is inconvenient for residents without easy transportation.

“I wish they would adapt to electronic rent payments. Having to get money orders is too much, especially without a car.”

Aging spots

The property is modernizing, but some units and common areas still show their age, with occasional delayed repairs or broken features such as the dog park water fountain.

Westview Forest is a strong fit for families, pet owners, and renters who want affordability without giving up security. If you have frequent guests or more than one vehicle, ask exactly how reserved spots and visitor passes work. If pests worry you, consider an upper-floor unit and ask about the pest control schedule. Residents receive parking stickers, reserved spots are available for an extra fee, visitors need a pass, and cars without one may be fined. Motorcycle parking is also available.

Parking, pests on ground floors, and the lack of an electronic rent payment option. Residents say most issues are addressed promptly by management.

"Jessica has been amazing from day one—professional, patient, and always on top of things."

Many residents report roach problems. Several say pest control is paid monthly but was ineffective or unresponsive. One tenant described moving into a unit already "infested with roaches," and others said the problem lasted for months.

Grounds and maintenance

Reviewers describe dog waste, trash, and broken glass around the property, plus slow indoor maintenance. Residents also mention broken gates and random fire alarms that weren't addressed quickly.

Several former tenants report deductions they considered minor or unfair, such as "$10 for replacing two toilet paper rolls" or "stains on a wall." Some said they were charged more than $500 beyond their deposits.

Esperanza at Keith Harrow offers a few bright spots, including attentive individual staff, move-in perks, and open layouts. Why Ceiling Fans Matter in a Houston Apartment

  • Better air circulation: fans move air through the whole room, which helps it feel fresher in humid weather.
  • Lower energy bills: a fan can make a room feel up to 4 degrees cooler, so you can set the thermostat higher while using far less energy than AC alone.
  • Year-round use: most fans reverse direction so in winter they push warm air down from the ceiling.
  • Style: fans double as a light fixture or design element, especially models with lighting or dimmers.

Tips for Touring Apartments with Ceiling Fans

  • Confirm which rooms have fans. Some communities include them only in living areas, others in every bedroom.
  • Turn them on during the tour and check for wobble, noise, and whether the light kit works.
  • Ask whether fans are on a wall switch, remote, or pull chain.
  • If you love high ceilings, see our roundup of Houston apartments with high ceilings.

Frequently asked questions

Why are ceiling fans better than portable fans?

Ceiling fans circulate air evenly across an entire room and help your AC work more efficiently, so you can use less energy overall.

Are ceiling fans worth it if my apartment has central air?

Yes. They move cooled air more effectively, which lets you raise the thermostat a few degrees without giving up comfort.

How do I clean a ceiling fan?

Turn it off, then dust the blades with a microfiber cloth or fan duster. For a deeper clean, use a damp cloth with mild soap.

Can I install my own ceiling fan in a Houston apartment?

Usually only with your landlord’s written approval. It’s simpler to choose a community where fans are standard, such as Delray Apartments or Forayna Vintage Park.

The Positives: What Residents Appreciate

Convenient Location

Several reviewers like being close to grocery stores, shopping centers, and other everyday essentials.

“It’s close to several grocery stores/shopping centers… This home is the BEST home EVERRRR‼️” – 5 Stars

Some tenants describe the community as relaxed and calm.

“The apartments are decent and peaceful mostly.” – 3 Stars

Maintenance gets compliments even in otherwise negative reviews, which says a lot about how residents view the crew.

“Maintenance is GREAT! Very nice and on time responding to work orders.” – 1 Star

Opinions on management vary widely, but some residents single out Ms. Catherine and Ms. Astrid for their kindness and willingness to work with them.

“Ms. Astrid has always worked with me and been fair… I hope God blesses Ms. Astrid tremendously!” – 3 Stars

“Miss Catherine… is kind and gets things done in a timely manner.” – 5 Stars

The Negatives: Concerns Raised by Residents

Pest Infestations

The most frequent complaint is roaches and rats, with some reviewers also mentioning raccoons. Residents say their own efforts to control the problem were not enough and that management did not address it adequately.

“The rats and roaches are still having a party in the units.” – 1 Star

Frequent Water Shutoffs

Many reviews say the water is shut off multiple times a month, often without notice.

“They shut off the water at least 3-4 times a month… One time I had no water for a whole day.” – 1 Star

Sanitation Problems

Residents report sewage overflowing into the parking area and leaving waste and debris behind, adding to concerns about living conditions.

Management and Customer Service

While specific staff are praised by some, many reviewers describe management overall as rude and unprofessional, and some allege unfair, discriminatory treatment of certain residents. These are individual allegations, but the number of similar comments is worth noting.

Safety and Towing

Broken gates, car break-ins, and a general lack of security come up often. One reviewer mentions a shooting on the property, and others describe aggressive towing.

“Parking is a joke. They towed my vehicle in 7 minutes of me parking.” – 1 Star

Amenities That Have Not Reopened

Residents say some amenities, including the gym, have been closed for years with no updates.

“The gym hasn’t been opened in about 6 YEARS.” – 1 Star

What to Check Before Leasing at Serena Woods

If you are still considering Serena Woods Apartments, a careful tour can tell you a lot. These steps apply to any community with mixed reviews:

  1. Look for signs of pests. Check under sinks, inside cabinets, and along baseboards, and ask how often pest control treats units and common areas.
  2. Ask about water shutoffs. How often have they happened recently, and how are residents notified?
  3. Walk the parking lot. Look at drainage, lighting, gate condition, and posted towing rules.
  4. Confirm which amenities are open. Ask to see the gym and any other amenity listed in the lease.
  5. Read the towing and guest parking policy so you know exactly where visitors can park.
  6. Get promises in writing, including any repairs to be completed before move-in.

Yes. Residents mention the location near grocery stores and shopping, the peaceful atmosphere, the responsive maintenance team, and helpful staff like Ms. Catherine and Ms. Astrid.

Many reviewers call the amenities among the best in Houston, pointing to two pools, a well-equipped gym, and thoughtfully designed common areas.

"The gym and pool stood out when I viewed other apartments, and I felt the safety was top." (5/5)

If a great gym is a must-have, you can also compare Houston apartments with a gym on our map.

A standout concierge and friendly staff

Bryant, the mail concierge, receives glowing praise for his helpfulness and local knowledge.

"Bryant is probably the most helpful concierge I have ever met and knows everything possible about Houston!" (5/5)

A convenient central location

Residents appreciate how easy it is to get to dining and work from Memorial Drive. If outdoor space matters to you, see our list of Houston apartments near Memorial Park for more options in this part of town.

"Great apartment in an excellent location." (3/5)

Responsive maintenance

"Maintenance is responsive in that they will come to your apartment whenever there is an issue." (5/5)

Clean grounds and lease renewals

The property's cleanliness and upkeep add to its luxury feel and are a deciding factor for many renewals. Several reviewers say they have stayed longer than planned, and for some it is the first community where they ever renewed.

"This is the only one where I've ever renewed my lease." (5/5)

A secure feel

Several residents commend the property for its secure environment, mentioning gated parking and well-lit pathways.

"I felt the safety was top. You can tell they've put thought into making the community secure." (5/5)

Common complaints in Alexan Memorial reviews

Noise and sound transfer

Poor sound insulation is the most consistent complaint. Residents mention noise from neighbors and heavy footsteps from upstairs, and some attribute it to the building's wood-based structure.

"The structure is wood-based and all the sound transfers… You can hear all your neighbors coming and going." (1/5)

If you are sensitive to noise, ask about top-floor units and tour at a busy time of day, like early evening.

Move-out charges

While move-ins are generally described as smooth, move-outs get mixed feedback. One resident said they were charged for carpet replacement despite hiring a professional cleaner.

"When moving out, we kept the apartment clean and hired a professional cleaner… management replaced the carpet in one bedroom and charged us without consulting." (3/5)

Management changes

The original management team was praised for building community, but some residents feel impressions declined after later changes, particularly in how complaints are handled. Others cite rising rents and limited flexibility at renewal time.

Value for the price

Some residents feel the cost does not match the experience, especially given power and hot water outages, which reviewers say happen during adverse weather.

"For the price you pay, you expect more… Definitely expect to lose power and hot water for extended periods of time." (3/5)

Leasing experience

A few prospective residents reported unhelpful interactions with leasing agents.

"The leasing agent was unwelcoming and unhelpful, refusing to show us any apartments." (1/5)

Community events and modern features

In its early days, Alexan Memorial was known for resident events like open bars and chef-hosted evenings. Long-term residents say those events became less frequent as the community grew and shifted toward partnerships with local businesses, though newcomers still appreciate the effort.

The property also offers energy-efficient appliances and recycling options, which environmentally conscious residents appreciate.

Alexan Memorial pros and cons

ProsCons
Two pools and a well-equipped gymThin walls and noise from neighbors
Highly praised mail conciergeDisputed move-out charges
Convenient Memorial Drive locationPower and hot water outages reported
Responsive maintenance and clean groundsMixed impressions after management changes
Gated parking and a secure feelSome feel rent outpaces value

Smart questions to ask on your tour

  • Which units or floors have the least noise transfer?
  • How are power or water outages communicated and handled?
  • What does the move-out inspection cover, and how is carpet wear evaluated?
  • What are the current pet policies and fees?
  • Are renewal increases typically discussed in advance?

Documenting your unit's condition with photos at move-in is good practice anywhere, and especially helpful given the move-out feedback here.

Frequently asked questions

What amenities does Alexan Memorial offer?

Two pools, a well-equipped gym, thoughtfully designed common areas, a mail concierge, and energy-efficient appliances, plus recycling options.

Is Alexan Memorial pet-friendly?

Yes. Check with the leasing office for current pet policies and restrictions. You can also browse more pet-friendly Houston apartments.

Is noise a problem at Alexan Memorial?

Some residents report noise from thin walls and the wood-based structure. If you are sensitive to sound, ask about top-floor units and visit at a busy time of day.

Is parking available?

Yes. Gated parking is available, and residents have generally been positive about it, though some reviewers mention capacity could become a concern as the community grows.

What is the Google rating for Alexan Memorial?

It held a 4.1-star Google rating at the time of writing. Check recent reviews before you decide, since ratings change.

Is Alexan Memorial right for you?

For many residents, Alexan Memorial's amenities, location, and staff outweigh the downsides. If you are a light sleeper or want a hands-off move-out, weigh the noise and charge complaints carefully and tour before you commit. Nearby neighborhoods like Rice Military are worth a look too.

  • Ask about rules and maintenance. Find out whether firewood is allowed, who handles chimney cleaning, and what renter’s insurance the lease requires.
  • Plan your furniture layout. A fireplace wall affects where the TV and sofa go, so measure during your tour.
  • Consider shared fireplaces too. Rooftop and clubhouse fireplaces give you the ambiance without upkeep.

Even with a warm climate, Houston has cool evenings in the winter months. A fireplace adds ambiance and a natural focal point for relaxing or entertaining.

They can, since fireplaces often come with premium floor plans. Cost depends more on location, unit size, and other amenities, so compare a few options side by side.

Which of these communities have shared rather than in-unit fireplaces?

Windsor Memorial, Hanover Autry Park, Estates at Memorial Heights, and Duo West Champions highlight fireplaces in shared lounges, clubhouses, or outdoor spaces. The Carter offers outdoor fireplaces in select townhomes.

Why Renters Choose Apartments with Gas Stoves

  • Precise heat control: Flame adjusts instantly, which makes simmering sauces and searing easier.

Tips for Touring Gas Stove Apartments

  • Tour at the time you would commute. Traffic near the TMC changes by the hour, so do a test drive or ride at shift-change time.

Which apartments near the Houston Medical Center offer shuttle service?

Several communities here have pet amenities, including Regard (dog park), Vantage (dog run), Helix (bark park), and Plaza (private fenced yards). Always ask about breed and weight rules. You can also browse pet-friendly Houston apartments.

It is easier at communities near METRORail, like 8181 Med Center across the street from a rail stop, or at properties with shuttle service.

How to choose an apartment with a sauna

Houston apartments with a den give you a flexible bonus room for a home office, a workout corner, a reading nook, or overflow guests, often for less than the jump to an extra bedroom. Below are 10 Houston communities with den layouts, work-from-home spaces, or flexible floor plans, plus advice on picking the right one.

Floor plans change often, so always confirm with the leasing office which specific layouts include a den before you apply.

Why a Den Is Worth Considering

In an apartment, every square foot counts. A den is usually a smaller, open or semi-open room. It often lacks a closet or window, which is what separates it from a bedroom. That flexibility is the appeal:

  • Home office: a separate place to work that is not your couch or bed.
  • Gym or yoga space: room for a mat, bike, or weights.
  • Entertainment room: a game room or movie corner.
  • Guest space or storage: a spot for an air mattress or the things that clutter the rest of your home.

If you mainly need a workspace, our guide to Houston apartments with study spaces is another good place to look.

Citadel pairs spacious layouts with a den you can use for remote work, hobbies, or storage. Ten-foot ceilings and large walk-in closets make the whole home feel roomier.

If you want a den that feels like a cozy retreat, 4001 Midtown pairs one with a fireplace and a spacious patio. Community perks include a resort-style pool and BBQ area. Read resident feedback in our 4001 Midtown reviews.

Key features: Den, fireplace, large closets, vaulted ceilings, and a fitness center.

Forayna Vintage Park's den easily becomes a home office or small gym. Nine-foot ceilings, wood-finish flooring, open layouts, and large walk-in closets help, and a private balcony gives you a place to take a break.

9. Willow Ridge Apartments

Location: 12800 Dunlap St, Houston, TX 77085

Willow Ridge keeps things practical: select units have dens or studies, plus central air, walk-in closets, a breakfast bar, outside storage, mini blinds, private balconies, all-electric kitchens, and washer and dryer connections.

10. 9900 on Memorial

Location: 722 International Blvd, Houston, TX 77024

9900 on Memorial is set among lush landscaping with 11 resort-style pools and spacious courtyards. Interiors have large windows, custom wood cabinetry, vinyl plank flooring, full-size kitchen appliances, and double-sink vanities in select units. It is pet-friendly, with an updated fitness center, covered parking, and 16 on-site laundry facilities.

How to Choose the Right Apartment with a Den

Start with how you will use it

An office needs an outlet, good light, and some separation from the living room. A gym needs floor space. A guest nook needs room for a sleeper sofa. Measure your must-have furniture before you tour.

Check the layout flow

A den off the entry is better for work calls; a den open to the living area feels more like extra lounge space. Some communities, like Citadel, offer larger layouts with storage, while others, like 4001 Midtown, lean toward cozier dens with a fireplace.

Look at the amenities around it

If you will be home a lot, a fitness center, pool, or coworking lounge (like Lumen's) can make your den work harder for you.

Do not overlook storage

Dens often end up as storage rooms. Walk-in closets and built-ins, like Forayna Vintage Park's built-in shelves, keep the den usable.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a den in an apartment?

A den is a flexible bonus space, often used as an office, library, game room, or extra living area. Dens typically do not have a closet or window, which is what separates them from bedrooms.

Are apartments with a den more expensive?

They can rent for a bit more than a standard unit of the same bedroom count, but they are often cheaper than moving up to an extra bedroom. The difference depends on location, amenities, and demand.

Is a den good for working from home?

Yes. A den gives you a separate workspace, which helps with work-life balance. Ask whether the den has outlets and lighting where you would put a desk.

How do I find out which floor plans have a den?

Ask the leasing office for floor plans labeled "den," "study," or "flex," and confirm availability. A locator can also check current options for you.

How to choose a concierge apartment in Houston

  3. Check guest policies. Some buildings extend valet to guests; others do not.
  4. Test the package process. Ask how packages are logged, where they are stored and how you are notified.
  5. Match services to your routine. Pet owners should prioritize walking and grooming; frequent travelers may value package handling and valet most.

What do concierge services in Houston apartments include?

Typically, buildings with concierge service carry higher rents because of the added staff and services. Ask which services are included in rent and which are paid add-ons.

Valet handles vehicle parking. Concierge covers broader tasks like reservations, deliveries and resident support.

Can a concierge help with pet care?

Beyond the pool, there is a Sky Lounge with bar service and a game room with air hockey and skee-ball. Active residents will appreciate the indoor basketball court and virtual golf simulator.

5. Parkside Residences

The fitness center has modern cardio and strength equipment, and an on-site concierge and controlled-access parking add convenience. Shopping, dining, and entertainment are steps away. For resident feedback, read our Dominion Post Oak review.

How to choose the right rooftop pool apartment

A great pool is only worth it if you will use it. A few practical tips from our locators:

  • Tour at the time you would swim. Check sun and shade on a weekday evening or weekend afternoon, and see how busy the deck gets.
  • Ask about hours and seasons. Find out whether the pool is heated and whether hours change in cooler months.
  • Read the guest policy. Ask how many guests you can bring and whether you need to register them.
  • Check reservable spaces. If you like to host, ask whether cabanas, grills, or the deck can be booked for private events.
  • Budget for the premium. Communities with standout amenities often carry higher rents, so compare the full monthly cost.

Frequently asked questions

Which Houston apartment has the most unique rooftop pool?

Market Square Tower stands out for its glass-bottom pool suspended over downtown Houston on the Infinity Deck.

It varies by community. Some, like 7 Riverway, have heated pools, while others may adjust hours in cooler months. Ask the leasing office for the current schedule.

Do apartments with rooftop pools cost more?

Generally, yes. Communities with luxury amenities like rooftop pools tend to have higher rents, so weigh how often you will actually use the pool.

Can guests use rooftop pools?

Policies differ. Many communities allow guests when accompanied by a resident or registered in advance. Confirm the rules before you sign.

Latitude Med Center, at 1850 Old Main St, has an infinity-edge pool and offers shuttle service to Texas Medical Center locations.

A quiet, dedicated area for focus, good natural light, reliable internet, and enough outlets near your desk. A separate nook, den, or loft makes it easier to keep work and home apart.

Both exist. Some apartments, like 1414 Texas and One Park Place, include study nooks, while others, like Domain Heights, use open-concept layouts with room for a work area.

Furniture and decor are usually fine, but anything structural, like mounting shelves, typically needs approval from management. Ask before you drill.

Ask which provider the building uses and how they handle delicate fabrics, stains, and claims for damaged items. For anything irreplaceable, talk to the provider directly before you drop it off.

excerpt: Located in the heart of Houston, East Bend Apartments offer a modern lifestyle with immediate access to trendy spots like Market Heights and MKT. With an overall rating of 4.2 on Google, East Bend is popular among many for its convenient location, supportive staff, and upscale amenities. But no property is perfect, and residents have […]
content:
East Bend Apartments reviews are mostly positive: at the time of writing, the community at 1111 W 6th St held a 4.2-star Google rating, with residents praising the location across from MKT, the helpful staff, and a well-equipped gym. The recurring downsides are security, specifically gate problems and car break-ins, along with some complaints about finishes and common-area cleanliness. Here’s a balanced look at both sides.

Disclaimer: This article summarizes Google reviews and reflects the personal experiences and opinions of East Bend residents and visitors. The 4.2-star rating was accurate at the time of writing and may change.

East Bend Apartments at a Glance

DetailEast Bend Apartments
Address1111 W 6th St, Houston, TX 77007
NeighborhoodHouston Heights, near Market Heights and MKT
Google rating4.2 out of 5 (at the time of writing)
Amenities mentionedGym, pool, dog park, community events
Top praiseStaff, location, fitness center, fast maintenance
Top complaintsGate and garage security, finishes, common-area cleanliness

What Residents Love: Positive East Bend Reviews

Friendly, Professional Staff

Many reviewers single out leasing agents Kara and Phoebe as responsive, friendly, and quick to address concerns. One reviewer called the team “a joy to interact with,” and several say the office consistently provides good service to residents and visitors.

A Prime Location Across from MKT

The location is a major draw. Living next to the Market Heights area and MKT puts restaurants, shops, and entertainment within easy reach, which residents say makes daily life both convenient and lively.

A Well-Equipped Gym and Community Events

Health-conscious residents call the gym “well-equipped,” and community events get praise for helping neighbors meet and socialize. If a strong fitness center is high on your list, compare more Houston apartments with a gym.

Quick Maintenance

Several reviews describe fast maintenance. One resident said an elevator was repaired within hours, faster than they had experienced elsewhere, and another reported an air conditioning issue resolved promptly.

Modern Interiors

Some residents like the new finishes and thoughtful layouts, describing the apartments as fresh and modern.

What Residents Warn About: Negative East Bend Reviews

Security and Garage Issues

Security is the most common complaint. Residents describe an entry gate that breaks down frequently and is sometimes left open, allowing unauthorized access. Vehicle break-ins come up often, with some reviewers saying as many as 22 cars were broken into in one night. One resident also mentioned trespassing because of broken door locks.

Inconsistent Management Response

While many praise the office, others had poorer experiences. One resident said management was unresponsive about damage to their car after it was towed improperly. A prospective tenant described leasing staff allegedly dismissing them after they shared their budget.

Finishes, Appliances, and Thin Walls

Some residents say ceiling fans, washers, and dryers are loud or ineffective. One review mentions thin walls and “cardboard” baseboards, and others criticize flooring choices and fixtures they feel don’t match the rent.

Common-Area Cleanliness

How to judge a picnic area on your tour

Houston apartments with a spa put steam rooms, massage, and relaxation spaces just steps from your front door, so unwinding after work does not require a drive across town. Below are 10 communities across downtown, Montrose, Spring Branch, the Medical Center, and beyond that feature on-site spa amenities, plus tips for picking the right one and the questions to ask before you lease.

Houston apartments with a spa at a glance

1. Parkside Residences

Location: 808 Crawford St, Houston

Parkside Residences sits in the heart of downtown and offers spa facilities that work for a quick steam session to clear your head or a longer reset at the end of the week. It is a smart pick for professionals who want city energy outside and a calm retreat inside.

2. Lumen

Location: 2400 W Dallas St, Houston, TX 77019

In Houston's Montrose area, Lumen's spa pairs minimalist design with ambient lighting. The spa offers services ranging from massages to therapeutic treatments, which makes it a good fit for residents who want more than a gym and pool.

3. Avasa Spring Branch

Location: 1095 Brittmoore Rd, Houston, TX 77043

In the Spring Branch area, Avasa brings a cozy, resort-style feel to apartment living. Its on-site spa focuses on self-care, with treatments aimed at post-workout recovery and relaxation.

4. Bayou Park

Location: 4400 Memorial Dr, Houston, TX 77007

Overlooking Buffalo Bayou, Bayou Park has a spa designed around natural light and a serene atmosphere. It is a peaceful place to relieve tension without leaving home, with the bayou's green space right outside.

5. The Fountains at Almeda

Location: 9000 Almeda Rd, Houston, TX 77054

The Fountains at Almeda offers on-site spa facilities that make it easy to fit relaxation into a regular routine, whether you need an hour to decompress or want to make spa time part of your week.

6. The Ambrose

Location: 7055 Hollister Rd, Houston, TX 77040

In Northwest Houston, The Ambrose centers its lifestyle on well-being. Its spa facilities include steam rooms and a calm retreat for recharging after a busy workday or on weekends.

7. Folio West Houston

Location: 2525 Citywest Blvd, Houston, TX 77042

Located in Westchase, Folio West caters to professionals who value both productivity and downtime. Its on-site spa offers a refined environment, with options ranging from deep tissue massage to simple relaxation.

8. Latitude Med Center

Location: 1850 Old Main St, Houston, TX 77030

For anyone working long shifts in the Medical Center area, Latitude Med Center's spa offerings, including hot stone massages, skin treatments, and aromatherapy, focus on holistic wellness. It is a welcome perk for residents with demanding schedules.

9. Aspire Post Oak

Location: 1616 Post Oak Blvd, Houston, TX 77056

Aspire Post Oak offers curated spa services in the middle of busy Post Oak, with a variety of treatments designed to leave you refreshed. The location also puts high-end shopping and dining close by.

10. Hanover Autry Park

Location: 811 Buffalo Park Dr, Houston, TX 77019

Near Buffalo Bayou, Hanover Autry Park balances urban living with a peaceful retreat. Its on-site spa offers personalized treatments, from massages to aromatherapy, for residents who want work and wellness in balance.

How to choose the best Houston apartment with a spa

"Spa" can mean anything from a steam room to bookable massage services, so it pays to look closely. Ask yourself:

  1. Location: Do you want to be in the middle of downtown or Post Oak, or would you prefer a quieter setting like Spring Branch or Northwest Houston?
  2. Amenities: Do you want spa features alone, or a full wellness package with a fitness center and pool?
  3. Usage: Will you use the spa occasionally, or make it part of your weekly routine?

On your tour, ask which spa features are included in rent and which cost extra, what the hours are, and whether anything needs to be reserved. Visit at the time of day you would actually use it to see how busy it gets. If heat therapy is your priority, also check our list of Houston apartments with a sauna.

Frequently asked questions

What spa amenities can I expect in Houston apartments?

It varies by community. Depending on the property, you might find steam rooms, relaxation spaces, or treatments like massage, aromatherapy, and skin care. Confirm the current offering with each leasing office.

Are spa services included in rent?

Access to shared facilities such as steam rooms is often part of the amenity package, while treatments like massages or facials may cost extra. Always ask the leasing office for details.

Do I need to book spa services in advance?

Shared spaces are often first-come, first-served, while one-on-one services typically require booking. Ask how reservations work before you sign.

Which spa apartments are near the Texas Medical Center?

Latitude Med Center at 1850 Old Main St is in the Medical Center area and offers spa services such as hot stone massages, skin treatments, and aromatherapy.

Which spa apartments are near Buffalo Bayou?

Bayou Park at 4400 Memorial Dr and Hanover Autry Park at 811 Buffalo Park Dr are both near Buffalo Bayou.

title: 10 Houston Apartments with High Ceilings and Open Layouts

description: Browse 10 Houston apartments with high ceilings, from Heights lofts to East End industrial spaces and lake-view homes. Compare amenities and find your fit.
excerpt: “High ceilings instantly change the way a space feels—more air, more light, more freedom.” This quote by architect Piero Lissoni sums up the allure of high ceilings perfectly. If you’re looking for a fresh, modern apartment in Houston that feels open, spacious, and vibrant, look no further than this list. We’ve rounded up the top […]
content:
Houston apartments with high ceilings feel bigger, brighter, and more open than their square footage suggests. If you want a home with room to breathe, this list covers 10 communities with soaring ceilings, from industrial lofts in the East End to lake-view apartments in northeast Houston.

For each one, you will find the location, what makes the space stand out, key amenities, and a map.

Why High Ceilings Are Worth Seeking Out

Extra vertical space creates a sense of openness that is hard to get from square footage alone. Taller walls make room for oversized windows, tall bookshelves, and statement lighting, and they help even a studio feel less boxed in. When you tour, notice how the ceiling height changes the feel of the living room compared with a standard unit.

Quick Comparison

CommunityAreaStandout feature

Alta Sunset HeightsNear the HeightsVaulted ceilings, industrial-chic design

Modera Garden OaksGarden OaksOpen-concept layouts, pet spa

Define Living at BrittmooreWest HoustonLofts with oversized windows, smart-home tech

Fidelis WestlakeNortheast HoustonLake views, yoga studio

1. Artistry Design District

Location: 3939 W 12th St, Houston

In the up-and-coming Design District, Artistry pairs expansive high ceilings with floor-to-ceiling windows that frame the city skyline. Amenities include a rooftop deck, a fitness center, and pet-friendly facilities.

2. Alta Sunset Heights

Location: 1617 Enid St, Houston

Alta Sunset Heights blends industrial-chic design with vaulted ceilings that make even studios feel grand. It is close to the trendy spots of the Houston Heights and offers a resort-style pool.

3. Broadstone Amelia

Location: 1610 Campbell Rd, Houston

Near the Energy Corridor, Broadstone Amelia uses high ceilings to let natural light reach every corner. Expect a spacious kitchen with sleek countertops and roomy balconies for unwinding after work.

4. Modera Garden Oaks

Location: 641 W Crosstimbers St, Houston

Modera Garden Oaks features soaring ceilings and open-concept layouts that are great for entertaining. Amenities include a resort-style pool, fitness center, and pet spa.

5. The Standard on the River

Location: 91 Jensen Dr, Houston

Overlooking Buffalo Bayou, The Standard on the River combines high ceilings with expansive skyline views. Residents get an infinity pool, coworking spaces, and a rooftop lounge.

6. Harrisburg Lofts

Location: 3530 Harrisburg Blvd, Houston

In Houston’s East End, Harrisburg Lofts has a true industrial vibe with exposed brick and soaring ceilings. Light flows easily through the space, making it a good fit for creatives and remote workers, and you are close to some of the area’s best dining and entertainment.

7. Define Living at Brittmoore

Location: 1888 Brittmoore Rd, Houston

Define Living at Brittmoore offers lofts with high ceilings and oversized windows for a bright, airy feel. Smart-home technology lets you control your space with ease.

8. Beckett Cottingham

Location: 13958 Cottingham St, Houston

Beckett Cottingham’s high ceilings and wide-open floor plans make furniture placement easy. This pet-friendly community has a pool, fitness center, and resident lounge.

9. Charleston at Fannin Station

Location: 9779 Fannin Railway, Houston

Near the Texas Medical Center, Charleston at Fannin Station is a commuter-friendly option with high ceilings in each unit. Amenities include a modern gym, resort-style pool, and green spaces. Read our Charleston at Fannin Station reviews for resident feedback.

10. Fidelis Westlake

Location: 12211 Summer Creek Trace Dr, Houston

Fidelis Westlake feels like a getaway, with high ceilings, large windows, and lake views. Amenities include a clubhouse, yoga studio, and outdoor grilling areas.

Tips for Touring High-Ceiling Apartments

  • Ask which floor plans have them. Ceiling height can vary by floor and layout, so confirm the specific unit, not just the community.
  • Check the cooling setup. Taller rooms hold more air. Ask about the HVAC system and look for ceiling fans to help circulate it.
  • Think about window coverings. Tall windows may need longer curtains or blinds, so ask what is included.
  • Look up when lighting is out of reach. Ask how high fixtures are replaced and whether maintenance handles bulbs.
  • Use the height when decorating. Tall art, oversized lighting, and large plants make the most of vertical space.

Frequently asked questions

Why are high ceilings desirable in apartments?

They make rooms feel larger and more open, allow for bigger windows and more natural light, and give a home a more upscale feel.

Do high ceilings raise energy costs?

Taller rooms have more air to heat and cool, so costs can be a bit higher. Ask the leasing office about the unit’s HVAC system and typical utility bills before signing.

Do all floor plans at these communities have high ceilings?

Not necessarily. Ceiling heights can vary by layout and floor, so ask about the specific unit you are considering during your tour.

Which of these are loft-style apartments?

Harrisburg Lofts offers industrial lofts with exposed brick, and Define Living at Brittmoore offers lofts with oversized windows.

content:
Tired of missed deliveries and porch pirates? Houston apartments with a locker system let couriers drop packages into secure, code-access lockers you can open on your own schedule. Below are 10 Houston communities with package lockers, plus how these systems work and what to ask before you sign.

Houston Apartments with Package Lockers at a Glance

1. Evolve Champions

Address: 14919 TC Jester Blvd, Houston

Evolve Champions keeps packages secure in a locker system you can access whenever it suits you. The community also offers spacious layouts and extra storage, handy if you have sports gear or bikes to store.

2. Modera Garden Oaks

Address: 641 W Crosstimbers St, Houston

In the Garden Oaks area, Modera Garden Oaks uses a high-tech locker system: you get a notification when a package arrives, and it stays secure until you pick it up, even late at night. Modern finishes and a community-centric vibe round it out.

3. Resia Ten Oaks

Address: 18036 Park Row Dr, Houston

Resia Ten Oaks offers an advanced, user-friendly locker system for quick pickups and fewer lost or stolen packages. The community also has a state-of-the-art gym and outdoor spaces.

4. Hycohen Residency Apartments

Address: 13511 Hycohen Rd, Houston

Hycohen Residency pairs contemporary architecture with a secure locker system that holds packages until you're ready. When you tour, ask to see the rooftop views.

5. Allora Bear Creek

Address: 11918 Clay Road, Houston

At Allora Bear Creek, a locker system means no standing in line at the leasing office for packages. Residents also get expansive green spaces and a pool.

6. Meridian City Park

Address: 2620 Almeda Genoa Rd, Houston

Meridian City Park's package lockers keep deliveries secure until you're ready. The community is known for large floor plans, making it a practical pick for families, couples, and roommates.

7. The Lively at Antoine

Address: 2102 Antoine Dr, Houston

At The Lively at Antoine, you simply enter your code to open your locker. The community is pet-friendly with landscaped grounds for walks. Compare more pet-friendly Houston apartments if that's a must.

8. Define Living at Brittmoore

Address: 1888 Brittmoore Rd, Houston

Define Living at Brittmoore offers a package locker system designed for 24/7 access, plus spacious floor plans. The location gives you easy access to the Energy Corridor and nearby dining.

9. Dakota at Shepherd

Address: 4840 North Shepherd Drive, Houston

Dakota at Shepherd's locker system takes the worry out of missed deliveries. The community also offers stylish interiors and resort-inspired amenities.

10. Fidelis Westlake

Address: 12211 Summer Creek Trace Dr, Houston

Fidelis Westlake's locker system is secure, accessible, and simple to use. Pair that with a fitness center, clubhouse, and nature trails, and it's an easy community to come home to.

How Apartment Package Locker Systems Work

  1. A courier or staff member places your package in an open locker.
  2. You get a notification, usually by text, email, or app, with a pickup code.
  3. You enter the code at the kiosk (or scan it), and your locker opens.

Some communities pair lockers with a front desk or concierge service for oversized deliveries.

Why Package Lockers Matter

  • Security: Packages sit behind a locked door, accessible only with your code.
  • Convenience: Many systems allow pickup any time, not just during office hours.
  • Fewer missed deliveries: No more coordinating with drivers or rushing home.
  • Less office back-and-forth: Staff spend less time sorting packages, and you spend less time waiting for them.

Questions to Ask Before You Lease

  • Are the lockers accessible 24/7, or only during certain hours?
  • How long can a package stay in a locker before it's moved?
  • Where do oversized packages go?
  • Is there a refrigerated locker for groceries or meal kits?
  • Is there a monthly fee for the locker service?

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a package locker system?

It's a secure, self-service set of lockers where couriers or staff store your deliveries. You receive a unique code to open your locker and collect your package.

Are package lockers safe?

They're much safer than packages left at a door or in a hallway, because each locker can only be opened with the recipient's code.

Can lockers hold any size package?

Most handle a wide range of sizes, but very large items may not fit. Those are often held at the leasing office instead, so ask how each property handles oversized deliveries.

What happens if I don't pick up my package right away?

Policies vary. Many systems send reminders, and packages left too long may be moved to the office. Ask the leasing team about their time limit.

How do I find Houston apartments with package lockers?

Start with the communities above, then ask a locator to confirm current locker setups and any fees at the properties you're considering.

image_alt: Houston Apartments with Pet Wash Station
content:
Houston apartments with a pet wash station save you from scrubbing muddy paws in your own bathtub, and they’re easier to find than you might think. Below are 10 communities, from Downtown and River Oaks to Memorial City and the Galleria, that offer an on-site pet wash along with dog parks, pet spas, and nearby trails.

Why a Pet Wash Station Matters

A dedicated pet wash station keeps dirt, fur, and mud out of your apartment and makes post-walk cleanups quick. It’s especially handy in Houston, where afternoon storms and park trails can turn a simple walk into a full bath. Stations are usually equipped with a tub and hose, so you aren’t clogging your own drain with fur.

Quick Comparison: Houston Apartments with Pet Wash Stations

CommunityAreaOther pet perks
The Driscoll at River OaksRiver OaksLandscaped walking areas
The McKinley Memorial CityMemorial City / Katy FwyPet spa, near Terry Hershey Park trail
The HayworthGalleriaDog park
Parkside ResidencesDowntownDog run, views of Discovery Green
Elison ParkWillowchase BlvdSpacious wash station for larger breeds
Hanover Autry ParkBuffalo BayouClose to Buffalo Bayou Park trails
Pearl RosemontMontrosePet-friendly common spaces
The CarterChelsea BlvdNearby parks and walking areas
San SimeonAllen ParkwayEasy access to Buffalo Bayou

Downtown and Inner-Loop Apartments with Pet Wash Stations

1. Parkside Residences

Address: 808 Crawford St., Houston

Parkside Residences puts you and your pet in the middle of downtown, with views of Discovery Green, a pet wash station for post-park cleanups, and an on-site dog run. It’s a strong pick if you love city life but want amenities built for pet owners.

2. Market Square Tower

Address: 777 Preston St., Houston

Market Square Tower is the all-in luxury option. This downtown luxury high-rise pairs a pet wash station with a pet spa, while you enjoy city views from above.

3. The Driscoll at River Oaks

Address: 1958 West Gray Street, Houston

In the prestigious River Oaks neighborhood, The Driscoll is a high-rise with more than 300 apartments, an on-site pet wash station, and landscaped grounds for daily strolls. It combines River Oaks charm with pet-friendly convenience.

4. Pearl Rosemont

Address: 2727 Albany Street, Houston

Centrally located in Montrose, Pearl Rosemont offers a pet wash station plus pet-friendly common spaces, with parks and trails nearby for walks.

5. San Simeon

Address: 2121 Allen Pkwy, Houston

San Simeon offers riverfront-style living with easy access to Buffalo Bayou for scenic walks. Spacious units give pets room to stretch out, and the on-site pet wash station keeps park dirt out of your home.

6. Hanover Autry Park

Address: 811 Buffalo Park Dr., Houston

Near Buffalo Bayou Park, Hanover Autry Park offers river views and a dedicated pet wash station. Spend the morning on the park trails with your dog, then rinse off on site. Read our Hanover Autry Park reviews for what residents say.

7. The Carter

Address: 4 Chelsea Boulevard, Houston

The Carter pairs its pet wash station with city views, a rooftop pool, and a fitness center. Nearby parks and walking areas make daily outings easy.

Galleria, Memorial City, and Suburban Options

8. The Hayworth

Address: 1414 Wood Hollow Dr., Houston

In the heart of the Galleria area, The Hayworth offers a dedicated pet wash station, a dog park, a gym, a swimming pool, and spacious balconies for unwinding after a walk.

9. The McKinley Memorial City

Address: 9757 Katy Freeway, Houston

The McKinley offers a full suite of pet amenities: a pet wash station and a pet spa, plus a rooftop pool and fitness center for you. The nearby Terry Hershey Park trail is great for walking or running with your dog.

10. Elison Park

Address: 7575 Willowchase Blvd, Houston

For a quieter, suburban feel, Elison Park features a spacious pet wash station that works well for larger breeds, along with scenic outdoor spaces and a relaxed atmosphere.

What to Ask About the Pet Wash Station on Your Tour

  • Is it free? Many communities include it with your amenities, but confirm whether any fee applies.
  • Do I need to reserve it? Some stations are open access, while others require booking at busy times.
  • What’s supplied? Ask whether shampoo, towels, and a dryer are provided or if you bring your own.
  • Will it fit my dog? Check the tub height and whether there’s a ramp or steps for bigger dogs.
  • What’s the full pet policy? Ask about breed and weight limits, pet deposits, and monthly pet rent.

Pet Wash Etiquette for Apartment Living

  • Brush your dog before the bath to cut down on loose fur in the drain.
  • Rinse the tub and wipe down the area when you finish so it’s ready for the next resident.
  • Bring your own towels and a leash or tether to keep your pet secure while you wash.
  • Respect posted hours and any time limits, especially on weekend mornings when demand is highest.

A little courtesy keeps the station clean and helps the community keep offering it as a shared amenity.

Want more options? Browse all pet-friendly Houston apartments on our site.

Frequently asked questions

What is a pet wash station?

It’s a designated area in an apartment community for bathing your pet, usually with a tub and hose. It keeps your apartment clean and makes quick post-walk rinses easy.

Is there a fee to use an apartment pet wash station?

Many communities include access with their amenities, but check with the leasing office to confirm whether any charges apply.

Do these apartments have breed or size restrictions?

Each community sets its own pet policy, so ask about breed, size, and number limits, along with deposits and pet rent, before you apply.

Which of these communities offer a pet spa too?

Market Square Tower and The McKinley Memorial City both offer a pet spa in addition to a pet wash station.

They’re often overlooked, yet quickly becoming a must-have for renters who […]
content:
Houston apartments with a game room give you a place to play pool, settle a ping-pong rivalry, or meet neighbors without leaving the building. It is an amenity renters often overlook on paper and end up using all the time. Below are 11 communities across Houston with game rooms worth seeing in person, from Uptown high-rises to a family-friendly rental community in Katy.

Game Rooms at a Glance

CommunityAreaGame room highlights
The Tradition - Buffalo SpeedwayBuffalo SpeedwayPing-pong, near the pool and clubhouse
Anthology of TanglewoodTanglewoodBilliards, flat-screen TVs, lounge seating
Arrive Upper KirbyUpper KirbyVideo gaming, board games, chess
CrimsonGalleriaPool tables, plush seating, bar area
Hanover SouthamptonNear the Museum DistrictShuffleboard, foosball, neon lighting
7 RiverwayUptownPoker tables, consoles, next to the media room
The WestcottNear Memorial ParkClassic games and modern tech
One Park PlaceDowntownBilliards, chess, video games
Aspire Post OakUptownPool, ping-pong, video games
Ellison HeightsThe HeightsArcade games, shuffleboard, foosball
Covey Homes VentanaKatyBoard games, billiards, gaming stations

1. The Tradition - Buffalo Speedway

Location: 9339 Buffalo Speedway, Houston, TX

The Tradition's game room is sleek and spacious, good for casual gaming nights or competitive ping-pong. It sits close to the pool and clubhouse, so it is easy to move from game time to downtime. Residents looking for a real community feel can use it for a weekly poker night with neighbors.

2. Anthology of Tanglewood

Location: 504 Bering Drive, Houston, TX

Anthology of Tanglewood's game room is built around billiards, with modern furniture, flat-screen TVs, and comfortable seating. The upscale setting makes it a natural spot to entertain guests. If billiards is your game, see our list of Houston apartments with a billiards room.

3. Arrive Upper Kirby

Location: 3333 Lake St, Houston, TX

Arrive Upper Kirby's game room has equipment for both video gamers and board game fans, with a bold design that mixes modern and artistic touches. The room is often the social heart of the community, whether residents are on a console or playing chess.

4. Crimson

Location: 2220 Westcreek Lane, Houston, TX

Crimson's game room feels more like a high-end lounge, with pool tables, plush seating, and a bar area. It sits in the upscale Galleria neighborhood, so shopping and dining are close by too.

5. Hanover Southampton

Location: 5122 Morningside Drive, Houston, TX

Hanover Southampton mixes modern design with playful energy: neon lighting, sleek gaming tables, shuffleboard, foosball, and a stocked mini-fridge. It is near the Museum District, so an afternoon of culture can turn into a game night back home.

6. 7 Riverway

Location: 7 Riverway, Houston, TX

In Houston's Uptown district, 7 Riverway's game room includes poker tables and console gaming setups. It sits right next to the media room, so a movie night can roll straight into a friendly competition.

7. The Westcott

Location: 929 Westcott St, Houston, TX

The Westcott's game room is a social hub stocked with classic games and modern tech, equal parts cozy and fun. The building also has views of Memorial Park, one of Houston's best green spaces, for when you want to get outside after a game.

8. One Park Place

Location: 1400 Mckinney St, Houston, TX

One Park Place's downtown game room works for serious gamers and casual socializers alike, with billiards, chess, and video games. It is a relaxed retreat from the pace of the city.

9. Aspire Post Oak

Location: 1616 Post Oak Boulevard, Houston, TX

Aspire Post Oak's game room is chic and modern, with pool, ping-pong, and video games. Located in Uptown, it suits renters who want luxury living with plenty of ways to unwind at home.

10. Ellison Heights

Location: 510 W 20th St, Houston, TX

Ellison Heights gives its game room an old-school feel with classic arcade games, shuffleboard, and foosball, finished with contemporary decor. It fits right into the Heights, one of Houston's most sought-after neighborhoods.

11. Covey Homes Ventana

Location: 4019 Ventana Ridge Drive, Katy, TX

Just outside Houston in Katy, Covey Homes Ventana offers spacious living and a casual but polished game room with board games, billiards, and video gaming stations. It is a good fit for families or anyone who wants a quieter setting with entertainment close by.

Why a Game Room Is Worth Having

A game room gives you a place to unwind, socialize, and take a break without leaving home. It is also one of the easiest ways to meet neighbors, especially if you are new to Houston. And when friends visit, you have somewhere to host that is not your living room.

How to Judge a Game Room on Your Tour

  • Check the condition. Look at the felt on the pool table, the paddles, and the controllers. Well-kept equipment usually means a well-run amenity.
  • Ask about hours. Some game rooms close in the evening, which matters if you work late.
  • Ask about reservations. Find out whether you can book the room for a private party or game night and what the rules are.
  • Look at the location. A game room near the pool, clubhouse, or media room gets more use, but a unit right above it may get more noise.

Frequently Asked Questions

What games are usually in apartment game rooms?

Common options include pool tables, ping-pong, foosball, shuffleboard, arcade games, and video game consoles. Some communities also stock board games or poker tables.

Are game rooms open to all residents?

Usually yes, during set hours, and many do not require reservations. Some properties let residents book the room for large groups or events, so check with management.

Can I host a private event in the game room?

Many communities allow residents to reserve the game room. Ask the leasing office about availability, guest limits, and any fees.

Which game rooms on this list have video games?

Arrive Upper Kirby, 7 Riverway, One Park Place, Aspire Post Oak, and Covey Homes Ventana all mention video gaming setups.

Do all luxury apartments have game rooms?

No. Many upscale Houston communities include them, but not all, so it is worth adding to your must-have list if it matters to you.

description: Find 12 Houston apartments with walk-in showers, from rain showers in the Heights to spa showers by Lake Houston. Compare finishes, amenities, and locations.

content:
If you want Houston apartments with walk-in showers, these 12 communities feature them, from rain-shower setups in the Heights to glass-enclosed showers near the M-K-T and spa showers out by Lake Houston. Below you'll find each community's address, bathroom and kitchen finishes, and standout amenities, plus a quick table to compare them.

Houston apartments with walk-in showers: comparison

CommunityAreaShower featureStandout amenity
Artistry Design DistrictW 12th StDual shower headsPoolside jumbotron, Paw Spa
