1. Artistry Design District

Location: 3939 W 12th St, Houston

Walk-in showers here feature dual shower heads. Open-concept kitchens have quartz countertops, undermount sinks, and stainless appliances, while ten-foot ceilings and LED lighting make homes feel open. Amenities include a resort-style pool with private cabanas and a poolside jumbotron, a 24-hour fitness center, a Paw Spa, a co-working lounge, and an event stage for live performances.

2. Lockwood on Buffalo Bayou

Location: 733 N Drennan St, Houston

Lockwood pairs walk-in showers with stainless appliances, granite countertops, and bright, naturally lit interiors. It sits near Tony Marron Park and the Buffalo Bayou hike and bike trails. On site, you'll find a large community patio with bayou views, a fitness room, a business center, a playground, and acres of green space.

3. Evolve Champions

Location: 14919 TC Jester Blvd, Houston

Evolve Champions combines walk-in showers with stainless appliances, granite countertops, plank flooring, and private balconies. The community has a resort-style pool, a pickleball court, EV charging, a 24-hour gym, a dog park, and a large clubroom with a kitchen. Gated entry, reserved parking, and detached garages are available.

4. Broadstone EADO

Location: 2425 Bell St, Houston

In East Downtown, Broadstone EADO offers walk-in showers, subway tile backsplashes, granite countertops, vinyl plank flooring, and private balconies. Take in skyline views from the sky lounge, play shuffleboard in the resident lounge, or train in a fitness center with cross-training gear and Reflect fitness mirrors. A 24/7 parcel center and a rideshare waiting room add everyday convenience.

5. The Standard on the River

Location: 91 Jensen Dr, Houston

Standalone showers and garden tubs give bathrooms a spa-like feel. Homes also have quartz countertops, French door refrigerators, wood-style flooring, built-in desks, and closets with wood shelving. The property sits along the Buffalo Bayou trail with multiple access points, and the multi-level resort-style pool overlooks downtown. Add a resident lounge, co-working spaces, a pet spa with trail access, and garage or carport options.

6. Define Living at Brittmoore

Location: 1888 Brittmoore Rd, Houston

A wellness-focused community with stand-up showers, farmhouse sinks, soft-close cabinets, ceiling fans, and 9-foot ceilings. Amenities include a boutique fitness studio with meditation and on-demand classes, an infrared sauna, a cold plunge, a lap pool, a dog park, controlled access, EV charging, and a business center.

7. Dakota at Shepherd

Location: 4840 North Shepherd Drive, Houston

Dakota at Shepherd offers both walk-in showers and oversized soaking tubs, plus custom walk-in closets. Kitchens have quartz countertops, designer cabinetry, and an eat-in bar with pendant lighting. Outside, there's a resort-style pool, a fitness center, and a grill area, along with smart entry locks and EV charging stations.

8. East Bend Apartments

Location: 1111 W 6th St, Houston

Choose between the CONCRETE and HERRINGBONE design packages; both include glass-enclosed walk-in showers, quartz countertops, and ceramic tile bathroom floors. Kitchens have islands with plenty of storage, and homes include formal dining areas. Extras include a self-service dog wash, a cycle fix-it station, EV charging, a multi-level parking garage, and proximity to the M-K-T. See our East Bend Apartments reviews for resident feedback.

9. Fidelis Westlake

Location: 12211 Summer Creek Trace Dr, Houston

Near Lake Houston and Westlake Marketplace, Fidelis Westlake has a family-friendly feel. Homes feature luxury spa showers, granite countertops, stainless appliances, walk-in closets with built-ins, private balconies, ambient cabinet lighting, and a water heating system designed for endless hot water. The gated community offers a resort-style pool with Wi-Fi, a 24-hour fitness center, and a bark park with a grooming station.

10. Alexan Junction Heights

Location: 3003 Summer St, Houston

Walk-in showers with rain shower heads and floor-to-ceiling bathroom tile set the tone. Kitchens add quartz countertops, farmhouse sinks, gas ranges, and wine fridges. The two-story athletic club has strength and cardio equipment and a yoga/spin studio, the clubroom has a pool table, and the resort-style pool hosts outdoor movie nights on a large projector screen. Pet owners get two dog parks and an onsite pet spa.

11. Westover at West Branch

Location: 5550 Dancy Rd, Houston

This gated community offers walk-in showers, granite countertops, gourmet kitchens with under-cabinet lighting, built-in desks, framed bathroom mirrors, and wood-style plank flooring. A big draw is the outdoor patios with medium or large private yards. Amenities include a fitness center, a pool, outdoor cooking areas, an expansive dog park, a cyber lounge with co-working space, and a business center.

12. The Rosslyn at Garden Oaks

Location: 1011 W 34th St, Houston

The Rosslyn features spacious walk-in showers, quartz countertops, custom cabinetry, floor-to-ceiling windows, gas ranges, dine-in kitchen islands, and wood-style flooring. Amenities include a resort-style pool with private cabanas, a fitness center with a yoga and spin studio, a sports lounge, a resident library, co-working spaces, EV charging, a pet spa, and bike repair facilities.

Why renters love walk-in showers

Walk-in showers are easier to clean than a tub-shower combo, make a bathroom feel larger, and are easier to step into, which matters for anyone with mobility concerns. When you tour, a few things are worth checking:

  • Every bathroom or just the primary? Many floor plans put the walk-in shower in the main bath and a tub in the second.
  • Tub needs: If you bathe young kids, look for plans with both, like Dakota at Shepherd's soaking tubs or The Standard's garden tubs.
  • Water pressure: Turn the shower on during your tour.
  • Accessibility: If you need an accessible unit, ask the leasing office what's available and request specifics like grab bars or a low threshold.

Several of these communities are in or near the Houston Heights, so our area guide is a good next stop.

Frequently asked questions

What are the benefits of a walk-in shower in an apartment?

They look modern, maximize space, are easy to clean, and are easier to access. Many feature glass enclosures or rain shower heads for a spa-like feel.

Are walk-in showers good for families with kids?

They may not be ideal for bathing young children. Families might prefer floor plans with both a walk-in shower and a tub.

Do walk-in showers raise the rent?

They're usually found in apartments with upscale finishes and amenities, so those units may rent for more than standard ones.

Are any of these apartments pet friendly?

Yes. The Standard on the River has a pet spa, Alexan Junction Heights has two dog parks and a pet spa, and Fidelis Westlake has a bark park with a grooming station. You can also browse pet-friendly Houston apartments.

Can I find walk-in showers in accessible units?

Properties including Fidelis Westlake and Lockwood on Buffalo Bayou have been noted for accessible units. Confirm current availability and features with the leasing office.

Find your walk-in shower apartment

content:
Houston apartments with quartz countertops give you a kitchen that looks sharp and holds up to daily cooking. Below are 12 communities that feature quartz, from Downtown high-rises to Montrose, River Oaks, Uptown, and Memorial, with the kitchen details and amenities that set each apart.

Finishes can vary by floor plan or renovation package, so confirm that the unit you are touring has quartz before you apply.

CommunityAddressKitchen highlight

Kitchens feature custom quartz countertops and backsplashes, energy-efficient Whirlpool appliances, a quad-door refrigerator, gas cooking, gooseneck faucets, and soft-close cabinets. Bathrooms add frameless shower enclosures and Delta fixtures, and floor-to-ceiling windows bring in natural light.

Amenities include a 12th-floor sky deck with downtown views, a game room, and an entertaining kitchen, plus a 4th-level pool terrace with shaded cabanas, smart home technology, EV charging, and concierge services.

These Tanglewood-area apartments have quartz countertops in both the kitchen and bathroom, with modern cabinets, under-cabinet lighting, and designer fixtures. Oversized floor plans and 10-foot ceilings add a sense of space.

Outside, residents get sand volleyball and tennis courts, grilling stations, picnic areas, a business center and conference room, bike storage, and concierge services.

Expansive kitchens pair premium quartz countertops with gas range cooktops, custom soft-close cabinetry, and stainless steel energy-efficient appliances. Floor-to-ceiling windows, 10-foot ceilings, and wood-look flooring fill the living spaces, while bathrooms offer oversized soaking tubs and walk-in showers with mosaic tile. Select apartments have private terraces.

Amenities include a sports lounge, a library with a dual-sided fireplace, a pool deck with private cabanas, a 24-hour fitness club with on-demand training, valet parking, a dog park, and a pet washing station.

4. Parkside Residences

Location: 808 Crawford St, Houston

Quartz countertops and designer solid surface backsplashes meet Bosch and Thermador appliances, gas cooktops, and Nobilia European cabinetry. Apartments have 9- to 11-foot ceilings, wood-style flooring, porcelain tile bathrooms, freestanding tubs, and undercounter wine coolers. Select units offer multi-level lofts with electronic shades.

The rooftop pool deck looks out over downtown, a 43rd-floor observation deck hosts gatherings, and residents get a fitness center, co-working pods, and a connection to the Downtown Skybridge System.

5. Aris Market Square

Location: 409 Travis St, Houston

Every home has quartz countertops with natural stone backsplashes, Italian-made custom cabinetry, gas ranges, wide-plank hardwood floors, and LED cabinet lighting. Select units add 5-fixture bathrooms, 6-foot soaking tubs, private balconies, and walk-in closets with custom wood shelving.

The community offers a resort-style pool with cabanas, the Secret Garden patio bar, a vinyl listening room, and Bravery Chef Hall, a 9,000-square-foot dining experience. It is steps from Market Square Park and the METRO Rail. Read what residents say in our Aris Market Square reviews.

6. Camden Post Oak

Location: 1200 Post Oak Blvd, Houston

In Uptown, this 33-story high-rise features quartz countertops, double ovens, and French door refrigerators, plus hardwood floors, 10-foot coffered ceilings with crown molding, and floor-to-ceiling windows. Penthouse units reach up to 3,400 square feet, and floor plans range from one to three bedrooms.

Perks include a 24-hour fitness center with a yoga studio, a conference room, complimentary valet, concierge services, and valet dry cleaning. Browse nearby options in our Galleria and Uptown apartments guide.

7. The Susanne

Location: 3833 Dunlavy St., Houston

In Montrose, The Susanne pairs quartz and granite countertops with GE stainless appliances, gas range cooking, genuine oak hardwood floors, and kitchen islands with built-in wine chillers. Residents enjoy a heated resort-style pool, poolside outdoor kitchens, an outdoor fire pit, and a fitness center, with the Museum District, The Menil Collection, and the Museum of Fine Arts Houston nearby.

8. Village on Memorial

Location: 15200 Memorial Dr, Houston

This West Houston community offers a townhome-style experience with quartz countertops, white subway tile backsplashes, stainless appliances, farmhouse sinks, and designer lighting. Bathrooms have large garden tubs and marble vanities, and homes include oak hardwood flooring, elevated ceilings, attached garages, walk-in closets, and balconies or patios.

9. Alexan River Oaks

Location: 3015 Weslayan St., Houston

This smoke-free community features quartz countertops with tile backsplashes, farmhouse sinks, Shaker-style cabinetry, full-size washers and dryers, and walk-in closets. Select units add mudrooms, dry bars, and wine refrigerators. Bathrooms have floor-to-ceiling tile, rain shower heads, and Moen fixtures.

Amenities include a resort-style pool with tanning ledge, cabanas, outdoor grills, a top-floor sky lounge, an athletic club with a yoga studio, controlled-access parking, EV charging, and concierge service for packages and dry cleaning. Explore more nearby in our River Oaks apartments guide.

10. Catalyst Houston

Location: 1475 Texas Ave, Houston

In the heart of downtown, Catalyst combines quartz countertops with stainless appliances, hardwood-style flooring, large closets, and big windows with views of downtown and the nearby ballpark. Amenities include a resort-style pool with cabanas and grilling stations, a sky bar, a gym with a yoga studio, a pet wash station, 24-hour door staff, and a bike garage. See more in our downtown Houston apartments guide.

11. The Cabochon at River Oaks

Location: 2828 Bammel Ln, Houston, TX 77098

Homes feature quartz countertops, subway tile backsplashes, stainless steel appliances, floor-to-ceiling windows with skyline views, plank-style flooring, and walk-in closets with custom organizers. The gated community has a pool, outdoor grilling stations, a pet park, a fitness center, and a business lounge.

12. Azure Houston Apartments

Location: 1111 Durham Dr, Houston, TX 77007

Spacious gourmet kitchens have quartz countertops, custom cabinetry, and stainless appliances, and homes include private patios or balconies. Amenities include a rooftop deck, a pool, a fire pit, a clubhouse with multiple lounges, a business center, a 24-hour fitness center, a pet grooming area, controlled-access parking, and automated package systems.

Why Renters Love Quartz Countertops

  • Non-porous: Quartz resists stains and bacteria, so spills wipe up easily.
  • Durable: It holds up well to scratches and everyday wear. Still use trivets for hot pans.
  • Low maintenance: Mild soap and water is usually all it needs, with no sealing.
  • Design range: It comes in many colors and patterns to match different styles.

When you tour, check the counter space around the stove and sink, not just the island. That is where you will actually prep food.

Frequently Asked Questions

How does quartz compare to granite or marble?

Quartz is engineered to be non-porous, so it is more resistant to stains and moisture and needs less maintenance than natural stone.

Do apartments with quartz countertops cost more?

Quartz is common in luxury and newer communities, which may rent for more. Some older communities add it in renovated units, so ask about upgraded floor plans.

Which Houston neighborhoods have apartments with quartz countertops?

This list includes communities in Downtown, Montrose, River Oaks, Uptown near the Galleria, Memorial, and the Heights area.

Are quartz countertops good for families with kids?

Yes. They are durable and easy to clean, which helps with everyday spills.

The Westcott offers both a billiards room and a golf simulator.

Is a billiards room the same as a game room?

Not always. Some communities have a dedicated billiards room, while others include a pool table inside a broader game room or clubhouse.

title: Tax Credit Apartments in Houston: 10 Options and How to Qualify

description: Tax credit apartments in Houston explained: who qualifies, what documents you need, and 10 affordable communities from the Museum District to North Houston.
excerpt: Houston is home to over 2.3 million people and growing fast. With such rapid expansion, finding affordable housing has become a top priority for many. Here’s an eye-opener: Did you know that Houston’s average rent for a one-bedroom apartment sits at around $1,300? That’s where tax credit apartments step in. These gems offer a more […]
content:
Tax credit apartments in Houston offer below-market rent to renters who meet income limits, and many look and feel like any other well-kept community. This guide explains how the program works and who typically qualifies, then walks through 10 Houston tax credit properties, from Museum District apartments to family townhomes with private yards.

Houston is home to over 2.3 million people and growing fast, and at the time of the original writing the average one-bedroom rent sat around $1,300. For many households, a tax credit apartment is the difference between stretching and breathing room.

What Are Tax Credit Apartments?

Tax credit apartments are properties built or renovated under the federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program. Developers receive tax incentives, and in exchange they set aside units at reduced rents for qualifying tenants. Many are maintained to the same standard as market-rate communities and come with solid amenities.

Who qualifies?

Eligibility is based on household income, typically between 30% and 60% of the area median income (AMI). Limits depend on household size, so a family of four can usually earn more than a single renter and still qualify. Each property verifies income during the application.

What to have ready

  • Recent pay stubs or other proof of income for every adult in the household
  • Photo ID for all adults
  • Recent bank statements
  • Information on any other income, such as benefits or child support

Ask each property whether you'll need to re-verify your income at renewal.

With access to the Texas Medical Center and downtown, Prose South Main is a strong option for healthcare workers. Energy-efficient one- and two-bedroom units feature stainless steel appliances and granite countertops, and the community is pet-friendly. See more apartments near the Medical Center.

In North Houston, Waterside Court Homes offers two-, three-, and four-bedroom homes with a more suburban feel. Every unit has a private yard, and there's a playground on site. The standout is how much space you get for the price.

How to Land a Tax Credit Apartment in Houston

  1. Check your eligibility first. Ask each property for its current income limits by household size and compare them to your gross income.
  2. Gather documents early. Having proof of income, IDs, and bank statements ready speeds up approval.
  3. Call or visit early. Affordable units in Houston fill quickly, and some properties keep waitlists.
  4. Apply promptly. Once you find a fit and confirm you qualify, submit your application as soon as you can.
  5. Compare beyond rent. Factor in utilities, commute, and amenities like laundry or a pool.

You can also browse income-restricted apartments in Houston on our site to see more options in one place.

Frequently Asked Questions

What income do I need for a tax credit apartment in Houston?

Most tax credit units are set aside for households earning roughly 30% to 60% of the area median income. Exact limits depend on household size and the specific property.

Are tax credit apartments the same as Section 8?

No. Tax credit apartments have reduced rents built into the property, while Section 8 is a voucher that helps pay rent. Some tax credit properties accept vouchers, so ask each community.

Are tax credit apartments lower quality?

Not necessarily. Many are maintained like market-rate communities and offer amenities such as pools, fitness centers, and clubhouses. Tour in person to judge condition.

Do tax credit apartments fill up fast?

Often, yes. Demand for affordable housing in Houston is high, so contact properties early and be ready to apply.

Valet trash is a doorstep pickup service. Rules vary by community, but the basics are usually the same:

  • You place a tied bag, often in a provided bin, outside your door during a set window in the evening.
  • A crew collects it on scheduled nights, typically several times a week.

13 Houston Apartments With Jogging Trails

On-Site Trail or Next to a Park?

There are two kinds of options on this list. On-site trails (The Hayworth, Brookdale West University, Fountains at Champions) are private and convenient, but usually shorter. Communities next to a major park (One Hermann Place, 2900 West Dallas, Village on Memorial) give you miles of path but you will share it with the public. Many runners like having both: a quick loop at home on busy days and a park for long weekend runs.

Tips for Running From Your Houston Apartment

  • Run early or late in summer. Houston heat and humidity are intense midday, so shaded trails and lit paths are worth asking about.
  • Walk the trail on your tour. Check the surface, lighting, shade, and how far it is from your unit.
  • Ask about pets. If you run with a dog, confirm the trail allows pets.
  • Have a backup. A gym with treadmills helps on rainy or storm days.

Which Houston apartments are closest to a big park for running?

On this list, One Hermann Place is across from Hermann Park, 2900 West Dallas is minutes from Buffalo Bayou Park, One Park Place is near Discovery Green, and Village on Memorial is close to Terry Hershey Park.

Look at lighting, shade, surface, length, and whether it is open to the public. Tour at the time of day you would actually run.

Houston apartments with school bus pickup make weekday mornings easier for families: your kids catch the bus close to home, and you skip the drop-off line. Below are 10 communities across Cy-Fair, Spring Branch, Klein, Alief, Galena Park, and Houston ISD where school bus pickup was reported, along with the family-friendly amenities each one offers.

School bus pickup apartments by district

CommunitySchool districtFamily-friendly highlight
Villas at CypresswoodCypress-Fairbanks ISDPlayground and picnic areas
Magnolia CreekGalena Park ISDPool, quick highway access
Trails of Timber CreekSpring Branch ISDFitness center, green spaces
Campbell GroveSpring Branch areaModern interiors, pet friendly
Lantern VillageHouston ISDOn-site day care center
Ashley CrestCypress-Fairbanks ISDAfter-school programs, pool
Ashford CreekAlief ISDPlaygrounds, large pool, family events
Willow BendKlein ISDLarge floor plans, nearby parks
Commons WestchaseHouston ISDOn-site library and study rooms
Kingswood VillageHouston ISDGated community

Bus routes and stop locations are set by each school district and can change from year to year, so always confirm the current stop for your child's school before you sign a lease.

1. Villas at Cypresswood

Location: 9844 Cypresswood Dr, Houston

Villas at Cypresswood is in Cypress-Fairbanks ISD, with school bus pickup at the community's entrance. Floor plans range from one to three bedrooms, which works for growing families. Kids also have an on-site playground and picnic areas, so there's a safe place to play without leaving the property.

2. Magnolia Creek

Location: 799 Normandy, Houston

Magnolia Creek serves families in Galena Park ISD. School bus pickup is a big help for working parents, and quick highway access makes commuting easier. The community pool is a welcome break from the Houston heat.

3. Trails of Timber Creek

Location: 5315 Timber Creek Place, Houston

Set in a quiet neighborhood near Spring Branch ISD schools, Trails of Timber Creek has a school bus stop that makes mornings simpler. The community also offers a fitness center and green spaces.

4. Campbell Grove

Location: 1515 Campbell, Houston

In the Spring Branch area, Campbell Grove offers on-site school bus pickup, so parents can skip the early-morning school run. Modern interiors and a pet-friendly policy make it a strong all-around choice for families.

5. Lantern Village

Location: 5815 Gulfton, Houston

In Southwest Houston, Lantern Village offers school bus access for Houston ISD families and several layouts for large or small households. The standout for working parents is the on-site day care center.

6. Ashley Crest

Location: 11900 Barwood Bend, Houston

Another Cypress-Fairbanks ISD option, Ashley Crest pairs school bus pickup with spacious units, a swimming pool, and after-school programs that keep kids engaged.

7. Ashford Creek

Location: 3803 Synott Rd, Houston

For Alief ISD families, Ashford Creek offers regular school bus pickups. Playgrounds, a large pool, and family-focused events throughout the year give it a strong community feel.

8. Willow Bend

Location: 13949 Bammel North Houston Rd, Houston

Willow Bend is in Klein ISD and offers direct access to bus pickups in a quiet neighborhood. Large floor plans and nearby parks make it a good fit for families who need room.

9. Commons Westchase

Location: 10751 Meadowglen Ln, Houston

Commons Westchase serves Houston ISD families with school bus pickup right outside. It's near schools, shopping centers, and medical facilities, and the on-site library and study rooms give kids a quiet place to do homework.

10. Kingswood Village

Location: 3233 Mangum, Houston

In Houston ISD, Kingswood Village offers easy access to schools, shopping, and public transportation, plus school bus pickup. Families highlight the secure, gated community, spacious units, and on-site amenities.

How to confirm school bus pickup before you lease

A leasing office can tell you where buses usually stop, but the district has the final say. Here's how to make sure the bus will work for your family:

  1. Get the exact address of the unit and look up your zoned schools on the district's website.
  2. Call the district's transportation department to confirm the stop location and pickup times for each child's grade.
  3. Ask the leasing office where the stop is: at the entrance, inside the gate, or down the street.
  4. Walk the route from your building to the stop, ideally at the time your kids would leave.
  5. Ask about after-school options like programs, playgrounds, or study rooms if your kids will be home before you.

Families often need extra space, so browse 3-bedroom apartments in Houston or 2-bedroom apartments. If you're focused on Cy-Fair, our Cypress, TX apartments guide covers the area in more detail.

Frequently asked questions

Do apartment communities provide the school bus?

No. School buses are run by the school district. A community can tell you where the stop has been, but you should confirm current routes with the district.

Which of these apartments are in Cypress-Fairbanks ISD?

Villas at Cypresswood and Ashley Crest are both in Cypress-Fairbanks ISD.

Are there Houston ISD apartments with school bus pickup?

Yes. Lantern Village, Commons Westchase, and Kingswood Village are all in Houston ISD and have reported school bus access.

Which communities have extras for kids?

Lantern Village has an on-site day care center, Ashley Crest offers after-school programs, Commons Westchase has a library and study rooms, and Villas at Cypresswood and Ashford Creek have playgrounds.

Are any of these pet friendly?

Campbell Grove is noted for its pet-friendly policy. Ask each community about its pet rules and fees.

content:
Houston apartments with senior discounts can make a real difference on a fixed income, and many communities offer them, though not always on their websites. Below are 10 Houston-area communities known for senior discounts, from waterfront Clear Lake to west Houston and the medical district, plus the questions to ask so you get the best rate.

More than 12% of Houston's population is over 60, so senior-friendly housing is in demand. Discounts change often, so confirm current terms with each leasing office.

Senior Discount Apartments at a Glance

Clear Lake Place18707 Egret Bay BlvdWaterfront views, quiet suburb

1. Clear Lake Place: Waterfront Living

At 18707 Egret Bay Blvd, Clear Lake Place offers waterfront views and a quiet suburban feel, with shopping and dining close by. Seniors can get discounted rates along with large walk-in closets, community events, and a pool that is great for low-impact exercise.

Tip: Ask whether longer leases come with a better senior rate. Many communities reward residents who plan to stay a while.

2. Trails at Lake Houston: Nature at Your Door

At 13922 Woodson Park Drive, Trails at Lake Houston surrounds residents with lush trees and walking trails. Apartments are modern and spacious, and the community includes a fitness center and a community garden for keeping up with hobbies.

3. Villas at Cypresswood: Quiet With Easy Access

At 9844 Cypresswood Dr, this community sits in a quiet neighborhood near essential services. It offers a resort-style pool, a fitness center, and a pet-friendly policy for seniors who will not leave their companions behind.

4. Magnolia Creek: Upscale Features for Less

At 799 Normandy, Magnolia Creek pairs senior discounts with stainless steel appliances, granite countertops, and in-unit washers and dryers. Regular community events and large patios or balconies make it a good fit for social residents.

5. Live Oak: Central Location With Elevators

At 851 Threadneedle St, Live Oak offers easy access to shopping, healthcare, and dining. Elevators, spacious units, and common areas make it senior-friendly, and amenities include pools, a business center, and a fitness studio.

6. Summer Creek: West Houston Retreat

At 9220 Clarewood in west Houston, Summer Creek offers senior discounts along with gated access, a pool, and large floor plans. Ask about specials on larger units if you want extra space.

7. Falls of West Oaks: Room to Spread Out

At 4034 S Highway 6, Falls of West Oaks offers large one- and two-bedroom units, two pools, a fitness center, and a picnic area, with shopping and dining nearby.

8. Windfern Meadows: Budget-Friendly

At 12919 Windfern Rd, Windfern Meadows is one of the more affordable senior discount options. Practical living spaces come with laundry facilities and a dog park. It is farther from central Houston, but that means quiet living and lower rent.

9. Harvest Hill: Close to the Medical District

At 8282 Cambridge, Harvest Hill is minutes from Houston's medical district, ideal if you have frequent appointments. On-site you will find a pool, a fitness center, and 24-hour maintenance. For more options nearby, see our Medical Center apartments guide.

10. Aero On Upper Bay: A Little Luxury

At 18290 Upper Bay Rd, Aero On Upper Bay offers serene views, a rooftop deck, a fitness center, and a private movie theater. It is more upscale, but senior discounts help make it attainable.

Choosing the Right Fit

If you love being near the water: Clear Lake Place offers waterfront views, and Aero On Upper Bay adds serene views with more upscale amenities.

If you want to stay active outdoors: Trails at Lake Houston has walking trails and a community garden, and Falls of West Oaks has two pools and a picnic area.

If healthcare access comes first: Harvest Hill is minutes from the medical district, and Live Oak offers easy access to healthcare along with elevators.

If budget is the deciding factor: Windfern Meadows is one of the more affordable options, trading a longer drive to central Houston for lower rent.

How to Get the Best Senior Apartment Deal

  • Ask directly. Many senior discounts are not advertised. Ask every leasing office.
  • Confirm the details. Ask the minimum age, what proof is needed, and whether the discount applies to rent, fees, or both.
  • Ask about renewals. Find out whether the discount carries over when you renew.
  • Stack savings. Check whether a senior rate can combine with current move-in specials.
  • Look at income-based options too. If you are on a fixed income, income-restricted apartments may offer lower rents.
  • Check accessibility. Look for elevators or ground-floor units, parking close to your door, and walk-in showers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do Houston apartments really offer senior discounts?

Yes, many do, including the communities above, but terms vary and change. Many offer unadvertised specials, so always ask the leasing office.

Which senior discount apartments are near the medical district?

Harvest Hill at 8282 Cambridge is minutes from Houston's medical district.

Which options are the most budget-friendly?

Windfern Meadows is one of the more affordable choices on this list, and Falls of West Oaks offers large units at discounted senior prices.

Are any of these communities pet-friendly?

Villas at Cypresswood has a pet-friendly policy, and Windfern Meadows has a dog park. Confirm pet fees and restrictions with each property.

content:
A broken lease makes apartment hunting harder, but it does not have to end your search. Some Houston apartments that accept broken leases will approve you if you explain what happened, show stable income and, in some cases, pay a higher deposit. Below are 10 communities we have highlighted as open to working with renters who have a past lease break, plus a plan to strengthen your application.

How Houston apartments handle broken leases

Not every community will rent to someone with a broken lease. Some are strict about credit and rental history; others take a more flexible approach, especially if you can explain the situation or offer a larger deposit. Screening criteria differ by property and can change, so treat any list as a starting point and confirm current policies with the leasing office before you apply.

Things that typically help:

  • A clear, honest explanation of why the lease was broken
  • Proof of stable, sufficient income
  • Willingness to pay a higher security deposit
  • A cosigner or guarantor with strong credit
  • Paying off any balance owed to the previous landlord

Apartments that accept broken leases at a glance

Every community on this list also features a golf simulator. If that amenity matters to you, see our full guide to Houston apartments with a golf simulator.

1. The Village of River Oaks

Address: 1015 South Shepherd Drive, Houston

In the upscale River Oaks neighborhood, The Village of River Oaks has been open to applicants with past lease issues who come with a good explanation and a willingness to pay a higher deposit. Residents enjoy manicured grounds, a golf simulator and high-end shopping and dining nearby.

2. Arrive Upper Kirby

Address: 3333 Lake St, Houston

Arrive Upper Kirby has been known to work with renters who have broken leases. Upper Kirby is known for its culture and dining, and residents get a golf simulator with skyline views.

3. The Museum Tower

Address: 4899 Montrose, Houston

In the heart of the Museum District, The Museum Tower has policies in place to help renters with broken leases. The community features a rooftop pool and a golf simulator, with galleries close by.

4. The Residences at La Colombe d’Or

Address: 3411 Yoakum Blvd, Houston

This boutique community pairs curated art collections and high-end finishes with flexibility for renters with prior lease challenges. It also has a golf simulator. Be upfront about your history here; the community is known for working with a variety of situations.

5. East Heights

Address: 784 Strawberry Pines Ct, Houston

In the East End, East Heights is willing to consider applicants with past lease breaks. Expect modern, spacious apartments, a community golf simulator and easy access to downtown and East End developments.

6. Hanover Southampton

Address: 5122 Morningside Drive, Houston

Near Rice Village, Hanover Southampton offers flexibility for renters with past rental challenges, including broken leases. Its golf simulator is a popular amenity, and shopping, dining and entertainment are within walking distance.

7. 7 Riverway

Address: 7 Riverway, Houston

7 Riverway is known for flexible rental policies and is open to working with renters who have had previous lease issues. Amenities include a golf simulator and access to Memorial Park.

8. The Westcott

Address: 929 Westcott St, Houston

The Westcott is known for working with renters who have previous lease breaks. It sits near Memorial Park, with strong views and a golf simulator for unwinding after a long day.

9. The Driscoll at River Oaks

Address: 1958 West Gray Street, Houston

River Oaks is one of Houston’s most sought-after neighborhoods, and The Driscoll’s application process considers a range of factors, including broken leases. It is known for giving second chances, and residents get luxury amenities including a golf simulator.

10. One Park Place

Address: 1400 McKinney St, Houston

This downtown Houston high-rise is open to applicants with past rental issues. Residents enjoy views of the downtown skyline and nearby Discovery Green, plus a golf simulator.

How to get approved with a broken lease

  1. Be honest. Disclose your rental history upfront. It will likely show up in screening anyway, and surprises hurt more than the lease break itself.
  2. Have your explanation ready. If a job transfer, medical issue or other hardship caused the break, explain it clearly and briefly, in writing if possible.
  3. Offer a higher security deposit. Many communities will accept a larger deposit to offset the risk.
  4. Show stable income. Bring recent pay stubs, an offer letter or bank statements that show your situation has improved.
  5. Line up a cosigner. A cosigner or guarantor with strong credit can ease a landlord’s concerns.
  6. Settle what you owe. If you have a balance with a previous landlord, paying it or setting up a payment plan, and keeping proof, can make a real difference.

Want to know what to expect from our side? Read how our free locating process works or browse our frequently asked questions.

Frequently asked questions

Can I rent an apartment in Houston with a broken lease on my record?

Yes. While some communities have strict rental history requirements, many are more lenient if you can provide a valid explanation, offer a higher deposit or show proof of stable income.

Will I need a higher security deposit?

Often, yes. The amount varies by property, so ask the leasing office about its policy before you apply.

Are there luxury apartments in Houston that accept broken leases?

Yes. Communities such as The Village of River Oaks, Arrive Upper Kirby and The Museum Tower have been known to be flexible with rental history while offering amenities like golf simulators and rooftop pools.

How do I find out which apartments accept broken leases?

Contact leasing offices directly to ask about their screening criteria, be upfront about your history, and consider working with a local apartment locator who knows which properties are more flexible.

Should I apply to lots of places at once?

Application fees add up quickly. It is usually better to confirm a community’s criteria first, then apply only where you are likely to be approved.

content:
Houston apartments with a golf simulator let you work on your drive or putting any time, without fighting the heat, the rain, or the drive to a course. You will find them in Uptown, downtown, River Oaks, the Heights, along Washington Avenue, and out in Vintage Park and Cypress. Here are 10 communities with on-site golf simulators and what else each one brings to the table.

1. Aspire Post Oak

Address: 1616 Post Oak Boulevard, Houston

In the heart of Uptown, Aspire Post Oak is a luxury tower with a top-tier golf simulator that recreates the feel of playing some of the world's most iconic courses. The building's sleek design and proximity to high-end shopping and dining add to the appeal. Practice your putting or work on your drive, then head to the nearby Galleria.

Why it stands out: An ultra-realistic simulator in one of the trendiest parts of Houston.

2. The Star

Address: 1111 Rusk St, Houston

In the heart of downtown, The Star blends historic charm with modern amenities. Its in-house golf simulator lets busy professionals keep their short game sharp without spending time traveling to a course.

Why it stands out: A building steeped in Houston history, steps from the city's major business hubs.

3. Hanover River Oaks

Address: 2651 Kipling St, Houston

Hanover River Oaks offers a cutting-edge golf simulator that delivers an immersive experience, whether you are prepping for a tournament or just unwinding. Residents also enjoy rooftop pools, an on-site gym, and panoramic views of the Houston skyline.

Why it stands out: Style and substance, with golf as one of several standout perks.

4. Market Square Tower

Address: 777 Preston St., Houston

Market Square Tower is famous for its sky-high swimming pool, but its indoor golf simulator deserves attention too. When it is raining, hot, or too windy for the course, residents can still get their swings in at this downtown high-rise.

Why it stands out: All-weather golf paired with sweeping views of Houston.

5. Lenox Oaks

Address: 3810 Drexel Dr, Houston

In Highland Village, Lenox Oaks pairs its golf simulator with a resort-style pool, a modern fitness center, and a dog park. Play a round with friends or perfect your technique solo.

Why it stands out: A balance of luxury and warmth for residents who like quiet refinement and staying active.

6. Mera Vintage Park

Address: 14914 Vintage Preserve Pkwy, Houston

Mera Vintage Park is a 55+ community built for active adults, and its golf simulator lets you practice your stroke, entertain friends, or enjoy a solo session. The property emphasizes top-tier amenities and a tight-knit community. If you are 55 or older, also see our guide to Houston apartments with senior discounts.

Why it stands out: Active adult living with high-end features.

7. The Madison

Address: 20130 Schiel Road, Cypress

The Madison brings high-end features to suburban living in Cypress. Its advanced golf simulator suits casual and serious players alike, and the elegant design gives the community a country club feel without the membership fees. Explore more apartments in Cypress, TX if you like the suburban pace.

Why it stands out: Upscale comfort without the city hustle.

8. Domain Heights

Address: 401 W. 25th St, Houston

In the Heights, Domain Heights merges sleek design with practical amenities. Its on-site golf simulator gives beginners and experienced players an indoor place to work on their swing.

Why it stands out: A fresh, hip vibe that draws a younger crowd.

9. Forayna Vintage Park

Address: 14818 Vintage Preserve Parkway, Houston

Forayna Vintage Park delivers suburban luxury with its own golf simulator for indoor golf any time of day. Vintage Park is already known for nearby shopping and dining, and Forayna's amenities take it a step further.

Why it stands out: A quiet setting without giving up luxury.

10. Modera Washington

Address: 2520 Washington Avenue, Houston

Modera Washington sits in one of Houston's hottest neighborhoods, close to nightlife and restaurants. Along with its golf simulator, residents get a rooftop pool and an on-site fitness center.

Why it stands out: A chance to mix socializing with practice.

Why choose an apartment with a golf simulator?

Convenience is the big one. An on-site simulator gives you practice time that does not depend on weather, daylight, or tee times, and it doubles as a fun way to meet neighbors. In Houston's summer heat, being able to practice indoors is a real perk.

Questions to ask before you lease

  • Is the simulator free to use, or is there a fee?
  • Does it need to be reserved, and how far ahead can you book?
  • Can you bring guests, and how many?
  • What are the hours, and is it available late in the evening?
  • Do you need to bring your own clubs?

Try to tour at the time of day you would actually play to see how busy the simulator room gets.

Frequently asked questions

Which downtown Houston apartments have a golf simulator?

The Star at 1111 Rusk St and Market Square Tower at 777 Preston St both have golf simulators downtown.

Is there a 55+ community with a golf simulator?

Yes. Mera Vintage Park at 14914 Vintage Preserve Pkwy is a 55+ community with a golf simulator.

Are there suburban options?

The Madison in Cypress and Forayna Vintage Park and Mera Vintage Park in Vintage Park offer golf simulators in quieter suburban settings.

Which golf simulator apartments also have a rooftop pool?

Hanover River Oaks and Modera Washington both offer rooftop pools, and Market Square Tower is known for its sky-high pool.

Do I have to pay to use an apartment golf simulator?

Policies vary by community. Some include it with your amenity package, while others may require reservations or fees. Confirm with the leasing office.

title: Alta River Oaks Reviews: What Residents Really Say
seo_title: Alta River Oaks Reviews: Resident Pros & Cons
description: Alta River Oaks reviews from residents: modern amenities and standout leasing agents, plus maintenance, build quality and management concerns. Read first.
excerpt: When looking for a new apartment, it’s essential to read reviews to get a real understanding of what the property offers. Alta River Oaks, located in a desirable area, presents itself as a luxury apartment complex, but opinions vary widely based on residents’ experiences. We will explore both positive and negative feedback shared by Alta […]
content:
Alta River Oaks reviews are split: many residents praise the modern amenities, clean common areas, and helpful leasing agents, while others report maintenance lapses, build-quality issues, and frustration with management. If you are weighing this luxury community, here is what Google reviewers say on both sides.

We summarized the recurring themes so you can go into a tour knowing exactly what to look for and what to ask.

What Residents Love About Alta River Oaks

Great amenities and an attractive property

Many reviewers are impressed by the amenities and describe clean, well-maintained facilities, appealing common areas, attractive outdoor spaces, and thoughtfully designed interiors.

“We went on a tour of the property and it was great. Great amenities, clean and upkept, and modern/updated.”

Standout leasing agents

The leasing team gets some of the warmest praise. Reviewers name Autumn and Lexi for patient, no-pressure tours that helped them find the right unit.

“Autumn did an amazing job at making me feel comfortable to ask anything… she did everything she could to show me anything that was available to my liking.”

“Lexi took the time to show me around, totally changed the direction of my housing search, and I definitely made the right decision!”

Clean and safe-feeling grounds

Cleanliness and a sense of safety are highlights for many residents and their families. One resident’s parent described Alta River Oaks as:

“a beautiful apartment complex, clean and well-maintained, and felt very safe.”

Prompt maintenance, when things run smoothly

Some residents report quick turnaround on work orders.

“Maintenance is always prompt with work orders, and the building common areas are always clean.”

Common Complaints in Alta River Oaks Reviews

Several one- and two-star reviews describe a very different experience. These are the themes that come up most.

Maintenance and security lapses

One resident said the maintenance team left their door unlocked all day after finishing a job.

“They left without locking my door. So my door was unlocked all day, and my valuables were left unsecured.”

Another resident’s refrigerator lost power after a hurricane, and despite repeated work orders and calls, they said the problem dragged on for about a week.

“We are now going into the weekend, and this will be seven days without me being able to store food… this is completely unacceptable.”

Building quality that does not match the branding

Some reviewers feel the construction does not live up to the luxury label. A long-term tenant who moved out cited frequent elevator breakdowns, dirty common areas, and a fire alarm that went off repeatedly without a lasting fix.

“This is not a luxury apartment complex. It is cheaply built and falling apart.”

Management frustrations

A former resident said management failed to address fire alarm and elevator issues and recommended against the building for that reason alone. Another prospective renter described a leasing office staff member as “smug and rude” and chose to look elsewhere.

“I do not recommend this building to anyone solely based on the management that currently exists.”

Inconsistent maintenance resources

Even some critics describe the maintenance staff themselves as “great,” but feel the team is not given the tools needed to keep the building in good condition.

Pros and Cons at a Glance

ProsCons
Modern, updated amenities and interiorsReports of slow or careless maintenance
Friendly, patient leasing agentsElevator breakdowns and fire alarm issues
Clean common areas that feel safeBuild quality criticized as not truly luxury
Some residents report prompt work ordersManagement responsiveness complaints

Is Alta River Oaks Worth a Tour?

If you value modern design, a clean environment, and attentive leasing agents, Alta River Oaks has a lot to offer. If reliable maintenance and solid construction are your top priorities, go in with clear questions.

  • Ask how many elevators the building has and how quickly outages are typically fixed.
  • Ask what happens after a storm or power outage, and how urgent work orders are prioritized.
  • Ask about the maintenance team’s staffing and how entry notices and lock-up are handled after service visits.
  • Walk the hallways and common areas on your own, not just the model unit.

To compare nearby options, see our River Oaks apartments guide, read Hanover River Oaks reviews, or browse our guide to luxury high-rise apartments in Houston.

This review is based on Google reviews and reflects the personal experiences and opinions of residents and renters at the time of writing.

Frequently asked questions

What do residents like most about Alta River Oaks?

Modern, well-kept amenities, clean common areas, a sense of safety, and friendly leasing agents such as Autumn and Lexi.

What are the most common complaints?

Maintenance delays and lapses, elevator breakdowns, repeated fire alarms, construction quality, and management responsiveness.

Is maintenance at Alta River Oaks reliable?

Reviews are mixed. Some residents say work orders are handled promptly, while others describe week-long delays and feel the team lacks the resources it needs.

title: Dominion Post Oak Review: Resident Pros and Cons

description: Our Dominion Post Oak review sums up what Galleria-area residents say about elevators, amenities, management, and location, plus what to ask on your tour.
excerpt: Dominion Post Oak is a high-rise apartment building in Houston’s prestigious Galleria area. It markets itself as a luxury residence, but its reviews tell a mixed story. Whether you’re considering a move or just curious about the living experience here, this blog will provide a detailed look at the pros and cons, based on real […]
content:
This Dominion Post Oak review sums up what residents say about the high-rise in Houston's Galleria area. Residents like the location, the views, the social events, and recent upgrades under new management, but long-standing complaints about elevators, closed amenities, smoking enforcement, and maintenance follow-through keep reviews mixed.

Everything below is drawn from Google reviews by renters and visitors, so you can weigh the pros and cons before you tour.

Dominion Post Oak Review: The Quick Take

What residents likeWhat residents dislike
Galleria-area location without heavy traffic at the doorElevator outages and long waits
Skyline views and a quiet environmentPool and dog park closures with little notice
Upgrades under new managementMarijuana odors despite the smoke-free policy
Staff praised by nameMaintenance requests closed without fixes
Resident events and pet-friendly policiesDated finishes for a building marketed as luxury

What Residents Like About Dominion Post Oak

Visible improvements from new management

Several reviewers say the new management team is making positive changes. One resident praised updated hallway paint and lighting, and said the elevators had improved too.

"The new paint pattern on our floor looks great and classy, and the new lights have made a big difference."

The same reviewers noted the elevators "all work, they are less noisy, and they show up a lot faster."

Helpful staff

Staff members Elijah, Tracy, and Jasmine are named in 5-star reviews for strong customer service during move-in. Jasmine also earns praise for detailed, informative tours.

"From day one, they've gone above and beyond to ensure a smooth transition into my new home."

"Jasmine provided an exceptional experience for me. Dominion Post Oak is very high on my list."

A convenient Galleria location

Reviewers like being near the Galleria without sitting in the thick of the traffic. One called the location "great without being too close to the traffic." Others mention skyline views and a quiet environment despite the central address.

Social events and a pet-friendly community

Residents mention events like holiday gift-wrapping stations and resident breakfasts. As one reviewer put it, the building is "pet-friendly and there are many social resident events."

Common Complaints About Dominion Post Oak

Elevator problems

Elevators are the most frequent complaint. Some residents say all three elevators rarely work at the same time, and one described waiting 13 minutes. Others say only one of the three works much of the time, leaving residents crowded and waiting. Since some reviews also report recent elevator improvements, ask for the current status when you tour.

"It's been 13 minutes, and I'm still waiting for the elevator."

Closed amenities

One tenant said the pool had been closed for over a year. Others said the pool and dog park closed without any explanation from management.

"We haven't received any explanation or even an email about why the pool is closed."

Smoking and safety concerns

A father of three described marijuana odors throughout the building despite its smoke-free policy and an incident in which someone vaping in a crowded elevator threatened him. He said the rules feel more like suggestions than enforced policies.

"Frequent marijuana smells and poor enforcement of smoking policies make it feel unsafe for families."

Maintenance and billing frustrations

One long-term resident said maintenance requests were marked "complete" without being fixed. Another was billed for water and sewage tied to a leak they didn't know about, and had to pay first and get credited later. A former resident said they were charged for damage after moving out and sent to collections without notice, despite having video of the apartment's condition.

"No one was willing to take my proof into consideration."

Not quite "luxury"

Several 1- and 2-star reviews say the building doesn't live up to its luxury marketing, citing outdated cabinets, broken appliances, and cheap carpeting.

Questions to Ask Before Leasing at Dominion Post Oak

  1. How many elevators are working today, and what's the repair timeline for any that aren't?
  2. Are the pool and dog park open, and how are residents notified of closures?
  3. How is the smoke-free policy enforced?
  4. Which units have updated cabinets, flooring, and appliances?
  5. How are leaks and utility overcharges handled?

Take time-stamped photos and video at move-in and move-out, and keep copies of every maintenance request.

Our Verdict: A Mixed Bag in a Great Location

Dominion Post Oak gets credit for its Galleria-area location, views, social events, and a management team that some residents say is improving things. But reports of elevator problems, closed amenities, weak smoking enforcement, and maintenance issues mean it doesn't always live up to its luxury branding.

If you want a high-rise near the Galleria, it may be worth a look. Just tour carefully, ask the questions above, and compare it with other luxury high-rise apartments in Houston before deciding.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is Dominion Post Oak located?

Dominion Post Oak is a high-rise apartment building in Houston's Galleria area. Residents say it's close to the Galleria without being right on top of the traffic.

Is Dominion Post Oak pet-friendly?

Yes, reviewers describe it as pet-friendly. Some residents report the dog park was closed at times, so ask about its current status. You can also browse pet-friendly Houston apartments to compare policies.

What are the biggest complaints about Dominion Post Oak?

The most common complaints are elevator outages, pool and dog park closures, marijuana odors, maintenance requests closed without repairs, and dated finishes.

Has Dominion Post Oak improved recently?

Some residents say new management has updated hallway paint and lighting and improved the elevators. Others feel the changes haven't gone far enough, so check conditions in person.

title: Most Expensive Area in Houston: Top 10 Priciest Neighborhoods
seo_title: Most Expensive Area in Houston: Top 10 Neighborhoods
description: The most expensive area in Houston is River Oaks. Compare the top 10 priciest neighborhoods by price per sq ft, median home price, and rent for renters.
excerpt: They say everything’s bigger in Texas, but in Houston, the price tags on luxury real estate often steal the show. According to a 2023 real estate report, Houston is home to some of the most expensive area/neighborhoods in the U.S., and if you’re looking for high-end living, you’ll be spoiled for choice. content:
The most expensive area in Houston is River Oaks, where the median home price was about $2.64 million and homes sold for roughly $638 per square foot, according to the 2023 real estate data this ranking draws on. The Texas Medical Center, Downtown, Afton Oaks, and the Greater Heights round out the top five by price per square foot. Below, we rank the ten priciest neighborhoods and, since most of our readers rent, show what median rents looked like in each.

Houston’s Most Expensive Neighborhoods at a Glance

Figures below come from a 2023 real estate report and were current at the time of writing. Prices and rents change, so treat them as a snapshot rather than a quote.

RankNeighborhoodPrice per sq ftMedian home priceMedian rentPopulation
1River Oaks$638$2,641,888$1,69721,154
2Texas Medical Center$490$551,835$1,43817,974
3Downtown Houston$481$2,301,345$1,61816,957
4Afton Oaks$327$924,496$1,5897,845
5Greater Heights$302$634,761$1,42638,477
6Fairbanks Northwest Crossing$287$280,128$1,27342,955
7Timbergrove$278$555,156$1,38236,979
8University Place$278$627,189$1,71519,686
9Oak Forest / Garden Oaks$270$505,349$1,18931,640
10Memorial$258$618,470$1,44241,121

One takeaway for renters: home prices vary far more than rents. River Oaks homes cost more than nine times what homes in Fairbanks Northwest Crossing do, yet the median rent gap was only a few hundred dollars a month.

1. River Oaks: Houston’s Most Expensive Area

Price per sq ft: $638 · Median home price: $2,641,888 · Median rent: $1,697 · Population: 21,154

River Oaks has long been the address for Houston’s elite. Expect sprawling estates, manicured landscaping, historic homes, and tree-lined streets where multimillion-dollar properties owned by business leaders and celebrities are common. Homes blend classical architecture with modern luxuries like marble foyers, infinity pools, and downtown views. If exclusivity is the goal, this is the neighborhood to beat. Renters can explore options in our River Oaks apartments guide.

2. Texas Medical Center

Price per sq ft: $490 · Median home price: $551,835 · Median rent: $1,438 · Population: 17,974

The Texas Medical Center ranks high on price per square foot thanks to demand from medical and research professionals who want to live near work. The housing mix leans toward high-end condos, modern townhomes, and high-rises, with parks nearby. See our Medical Center apartments guide for rentals in the area.

3. Downtown Houston

Price per sq ft: $481 · Median home price: $2,301,345 · Median rent: $1,618 · Population: 16,957

Downtown has transformed into a hub of luxury high-rises, upscale dining, and the Theater District. Condos and apartments offer rooftop pools and floor-to-ceiling windows with skyline views, and many residents walk to the office or hop on the Metro. Browse Downtown Houston apartments to compare high-rise rentals.

4. Afton Oaks

Price per sq ft: $327 · Median home price: $924,496 · Median rent: $1,589 · Population: 7,845

Tucked just inside the 610 Loop, Afton Oaks feels like a suburban retreat, with mid-century homes, expansive lots, wide streets, and mature trees. It’s popular with buyers who want space without giving up proximity to the Galleria, and high-end renovations keep prices climbing.

5. Greater Heights

Price per sq ft: $302 · Median home price: $634,761 · Median rent: $1,426 · Population: 38,477

The Greater Heights has surged in popularity. Victorian homes, craftsman bungalows, and new townhomes sit side by side, close to downtown and surrounded by cafes, boutiques, and parks. Homes are smaller than in River Oaks but still carry hefty price tags. Our Houston Heights apartments guide covers rentals here.

6. Fairbanks Northwest Crossing

Price per sq ft: $287 · Median home price: $280,128 · Median rent: $1,273 · Population: 42,955

Fairbanks Northwest Crossing lacks the name recognition of River Oaks, but its appeal is relative affordability. Many homes have large yards and modern upgrades, and highway access makes it easy to reach downtown, which is why it’s a favorite with families who want space.

7. Timbergrove

Price per sq ft: $278 · Median home price: $555,156 · Median rent: $1,382 · Population: 36,979

Just west of the Greater Heights, Timbergrove mixes mid-century modern homes with new builds. Spacious, tree-filled lots and access to the Bayou Greenways give it a quieter, more suburban feel while keeping inner-loop amenities close.

8. University Place

Price per sq ft: $278 · Median home price: $627,189 · Median rent: $1,715 · Population: 19,686

Home to Rice University and close to the Texas Medical Center, University Place has an academic feel and a mix of modern homes and charming older properties. Notably, it had the highest median rent on this list.

9. Oak Forest / Garden Oaks

Price per sq ft: $270 · Median home price: $505,349 · Median rent: $1,189 · Population: 31,640

North of the Greater Heights, Oak Forest and Garden Oaks offer similar charm with more space and slightly lower prices. Expect lush greenery, large lots, classic ranch-style homes alongside new construction, plenty of parks, and easy highway access. It had the lowest median rent of the ten.

10. Memorial

Price per sq ft: $258 · Median home price: $618,470 · Median rent: $1,442 · Population: 41,121

Memorial is home to some of Houston’s wealthiest residents, with grand estates and modern mansions. Families are drawn by highly regarded schools, and the area offers proximity to Memorial Park, high-end shopping and dining, and a manageable commute downtown.

Honorable Mentions

  • Tanglewood: known for large estates and lush streets.
  • West University Place: a top spot for families thanks to its schools.
  • Galleria/Uptown: a hub for professionals who want Houston’s best shopping and dining nearby.

Renting in Houston’s Priciest Neighborhoods

You don’t have to buy a $2 million home to live in these areas. Many renters get the address, the walkability, and the amenities for far less than a mortgage would cost. A few tips:

  • Compare price per square foot, not just rent. A slightly higher rent in a larger unit can be the better deal.
  • Look one neighborhood over. Timbergrove and Oak Forest/Garden Oaks sit near the Heights, and the median rents shown here were lower.
  • Ask about move-in specials. Luxury communities often run concessions, especially during slower leasing months.
  • Factor in commute and parking costs, which can offset a cheaper rent farther out.

Frequently asked questions

What is the most expensive area in Houston?

River Oaks, with a median home price of $2,641,888 and $638 per square foot in the 2023 data this ranking uses.

Which expensive Houston neighborhood has the highest rent?

University Place had the highest median rent on this list at $1,715, just ahead of River Oaks at $1,697.

Is Downtown Houston expensive to live in?

Yes. Downtown ranked third by price per square foot ($481), with a median home price of $2,301,345 and a median rent of $1,618 at the time of writing.

Which of these neighborhoods is the most affordable for renters?

Oak Forest/Garden Oaks had the lowest median rent of the ten at $1,189, followed by Fairbanks Northwest Crossing at $1,273.

Getting Around Houston From a Townhome

Houston is big, so location matters. METRO buses and light rail help renters in areas like downtown and Midtown get around easily, and the highway system keeps most destinations within reach if you drive.

  • Test the commute. Drive the route at rush hour before you sign.

Why choose a luxury high-rise in Houston?

What makes a high-rise "luxury"?

It's about quality, not just price. Expect high-end finishes such as granite countertops and custom cabinetry, modern appliances, and smart home technology. The amenities often set these buildings apart: an on-site spa, a heated infinity pool, or private resident lounges. If concierge service is on your must-have list, that roundup is a good next read.

How much do luxury high-rise apartments in Houston cost?
